reference: Sahih al-Bukhari, hadith 2661, book 52, باب تَعْدِيلِ النِّسَاءِ بَعْضِهِنَّ بَعْضًا
text_original: حَدَّثَنَا أَبُو الرَّبِيعِ، سُلَيْمَانُ بْنُ دَاوُدَ وَأَفْهَمَنِي بَعْضَهُ أَحْمَدُ حَدَّثَنَا فُلَيْحُ بْنُ سُلَيْمَانَ، عَنِ ابْنِ شِهَابٍ الزُّهْرِيِّ، عَنْ عُرْوَةَ بْنِ الزُّبَيْرِ، وَسَعِيدِ بْنِ الْمُسَيَّبِ، وَعَلْقَمَةَ بْنِ وَقَّاصٍ اللَّيْثِيِّ، وَعُبَيْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ عُتْبَةَ، عَنْ عَائِشَةَ ـ رضى الله عنها ـ زَوْجِ النَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه وسلم حِينَ قَالَ لَهَا أَهْلُ الإِفْكِ مَا قَالُوا، فَبَرَّأَهَا اللَّهُ مِنْهُ، قَالَ الزُّهْرِيُّ، وَكُلُّهُمْ حَدَّثَنِي طَائِفَةً مِنْ حَدِيثِهَا وَبَعْضُهُمْ أَوْعَى مِنْ بَعْضٍ، وَأَثْبَتُ لَهُ اقْتِصَاصًا، وَقَدْ وَعَيْتُ عَنْ كُلِّ وَاحِدٍ مِنْهُمُ الْحَدِيثَ الَّذِي حَدَّثَنِي عَنْ عَائِشَةَ، وَبَعْضُ حَدِيثِهِمْ يُصَدِّقُ بَعْضًا‏.‏ زَعَمُوا أَنَّ عَائِشَةَ قَالَتْ كَانَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم إِذَا أَرَادَ أَنْ يَخْرُجَ سَفَرًا أَقْرَعَ بَيْنَ أَزْوَاجِهِ، فَأَيَّتُهُنَّ خَرَجَ سَهْمُهَا خَرَجَ بِهَا مَعَهُ، فَأَقْرَعَ بَيْنَنَا فِي غَزَاةٍ غَزَاهَا فَخَرَجَ سَهْمِي، فَخَرَجْتُ مَعَهُ بَعْدَ مَا أُنْزِلَ الْحِجَابُ، فَأَنَا أُحْمَلُ فِي هَوْدَجٍ وَأُنْزَلُ فِيهِ، فَسِرْنَا حَتَّى إِذَا فَرَغَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم مِنْ غَزْوَتِهِ تِلْكَ، وَقَفَلَ وَدَنَوْنَا مِنَ الْمَدِينَةِ، آذَنَ لَيْلَةً بِالرَّحِيلِ، فَقُمْتُ حِينَ آذَنُوا بِالرَّحِيلِ، فَمَشَيْتُ حَتَّى جَاوَزْتُ الْجَيْشَ، فَلَمَّا قَضَيْتُ شَأْنِي أَقْبَلْتُ إِلَى الرَّحْلِ، فَلَمَسْتُ صَدْرِي، فَإِذَا عِقْدٌ لِي مِنْ جَزْعِ أَظْفَارٍ قَدِ انْقَطَعَ، فَرَجَعْتُ فَالْتَمَسْتُ عِقْدِي، فَحَبَسَنِي ابْتِغَاؤُهُ، فَأَقْبَلَ الَّذِينَ يَرْحَلُونَ لِي، فَاحْتَمَلُوا هَوْدَجِي فَرَحَلُوهُ عَلَى بَعِيرِي الَّذِي كُنْتُ أَرْكَبُ، وَهُمْ يَحْسِبُونَ أَنِّي فِيهِ، وَكَانَ النِّسَاءُ إِذْ ذَاكَ خِفَافًا لَمْ يَثْقُلْنَ وَلَمْ يَغْشَهُنَّ اللَّحْمُ، وَإِنَّمَا يَأْكُلْنَ الْعُلْقَةَ مِنَ الطَّعَامِ، فَلَمْ يَسْتَنْكِرِ الْقَوْمُ حِينَ رَفَعُوهُ ثِقَلَ الْهَوْدَجِ فَاحْتَمَلُوهُ وَكُنْتُ جَارِيَةً حَدِيثَةَ السِّنِّ، فَبَعَثُوا الْجَمَلَ وَسَارُوا، فَوَجَدْتُ عِقْدِي بَعْدَ مَا اسْتَمَرَّ الْجَيْشُ، فَجِئْتُ مَنْزِلَهُمْ وَلَيْسَ فِيهِ أَحَدٌ، فَأَمَمْتُ مَنْزِلِي الَّذِي كُنْتُ بِهِ فَظَنَنْتُ أَنَّهُمْ سَيَفْقِدُونِي فَيَرْجِعُونَ إِلَىَّ، فَبَيْنَا أَنَا جَالِسَةٌ غَلَبَتْنِي عَيْنَاىَ فَنِمْتُ، وَكَانَ صَفْوَانُ بْنُ الْمُعَطَّلِ السُّلَمِيُّ ثُمَّ الذَّكْوَانِيُّ مِنْ وَرَاءِ الْجَيْشِ، فَأَصْبَحَ عِنْدَ مَنْزِلِي فَرَأَى سَوَادَ إِنْسَانٍ نَائِمٍ فَأَتَانِي، وَكَانَ يَرَانِي قَبْلَ الْحِجَابِ فَاسْتَيْقَظْتُ بِاسْتِرْجَاعِهِ حِينَ أَنَاخَ رَاحِلَتَهُ، فَوَطِئَ يَدَهَا فَرَكِبْتُهَا فَانْطَلَقَ يَقُودُ بِي الرَّاحِلَةَ، حَتَّى أَتَيْنَا الْجَيْشَ بَعْدَ مَا نَزَلُوا مُعَرِّسِينَ فِي نَحْرِ الظَّهِيرَةِ، فَهَلَكَ مَنْ هَلَكَ، وَكَانَ الَّذِي تَوَلَّى الإِفْكَ عَبْدُ اللَّهِ بْنُ أُبَىٍّ ابْنُ سَلُولَ، فَقَدِمْنَا الْمَدِينَةَ فَاشْتَكَيْتُ بِهَا شَهْرًا، يُفِيضُونَ مِنْ قَوْلِ أَصْحَابِ الإِفْكِ، وَيَرِيبُنِي فِي وَجَعِي أَنِّي لاَ أَرَى مِنَ النَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه وسلم اللُّطْفَ الَّذِي كُنْتُ أَرَى مِنْهُ حِينَ أَمْرَضُ، إِنَّمَا يَدْخُلُ فَيُسَلِّمُ ثُمَّ يَقُولُ ‏"‏ كَيْفَ تِيكُمْ ‏"‏‏.‏ لاَ أَشْعُرُ بِشَىْءٍ مِنْ ذَلِكَ حَتَّى نَقَهْتُ، فَخَرَجْتُ أَنَا وَأُمُّ مِسْطَحٍ قِبَلَ الْمَنَاصِعِ مُتَبَرَّزُنَا، لاَ نَخْرُجُ إِلاَّ لَيْلاً إِلَى لَيْلٍ، وَذَلِكَ قَبْلَ أَنْ نَتَّخِذَ الْكُنُفَ قَرِيبًا مِنْ بُيُوتِنَا، وَأَمْرُنَا أَمْرُ الْعَرَبِ الأُوَلِ فِي الْبَرِّيَّةِ أَوْ فِي التَّنَزُّهِ، فَأَقْبَلْتُ أَنَا وَأُمُّ مِسْطَحٍ بِنْتُ أَبِي رُهْمٍ نَمْشِي، فَعَثُرَتْ فِي مِرْطِهَا فَقَالَتْ تَعِسَ مِسْطَحٌ، فَقُلْتُ لَهَا بِئْسَ مَا قُلْتِ، أَتَسُبِّينَ رَجُلاً شَهِدَ بَدْرًا فَقَالَتْ يَا هَنْتَاهْ أَلَمْ تَسْمَعِي مَا قَالُوا فَأَخْبَرَتْنِي بِقَوْلِ أَهْلِ الإِفْكِ، فَازْدَدْتُ مَرَضًا إِلَى مَرَضِي، فَلَمَّا رَجَعْتُ إِلَى بَيْتِي دَخَلَ عَلَىَّ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم فَسَلَّمَ فَقَالَ ‏"‏ كَيْفَ تِيكُمْ ‏"‏‏.‏ فَقُلْتُ ائْذَنْ لِي إِلَى أَبَوَىَّ‏.‏ قَالَتْ وَأَنَا حِينَئِذٍ أُرِيدُ أَنْ أَسْتَيْقِنَ الْخَبَرَ مِنْ قِبَلِهِمَا، فَأَذِنَ لِي رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم فَأَتَيْتُ أَبَوَىَّ فَقُلْتُ لأُمِّي مَا يَتَحَدَّثُ بِهِ النَّاسُ فَقَالَتْ يَا بُنَيَّةُ هَوِّنِي عَلَى نَفْسِكِ الشَّأْنَ، فَوَاللَّهِ لَقَلَّمَا كَانَتِ امْرَأَةٌ قَطُّ وَضِيئَةٌ عِنْدَ رَجُلٍ يُحِبُّهَا وَلَهَا ضَرَائِرُ إِلاَّ أَكْثَرْنَ عَلَيْهَا‏.‏ فَقُلْتُ سُبْحَانَ اللَّهِ وَلَقَدْ يَتَحَدَّثُ النَّاسُ بِهَذَا قَالَتْ فَبِتُّ تِلْكَ اللَّيْلَةَ حَتَّى أَصْبَحْتُ لاَ يَرْقَأُ لِي دَمْعٌ وَلاَ أَكْتَحِلُ بِنَوْمٍ، ثُمَّ أَصْبَحْتُ فَدَعَا رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم عَلِيَّ بْنَ أَبِي طَالِبٍ وَأُسَامَةَ بْنَ زَيْدٍ حِينَ اسْتَلْبَثَ الْوَحْىُ، يَسْتَشِيرُهُمَا فِي فِرَاقِ أَهْلِهِ، فَأَمَّا أُسَامَةُ فَأَشَارَ عَلَيْهِ بِالَّذِي يَعْلَمُ فِي نَفْسِهِ مِنَ الْوُدِّ لَهُمْ، فَقَالَ أُسَامَةُ أَهْلُكَ يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ وَلاَ نَعْلَمُ وَاللَّهِ إِلاَّ خَيْرًا، وَأَمَّا عَلِيُّ بْنُ أَبِي طَالِبٍ فَقَالَ يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ لَمْ يُضَيِّقِ اللَّهُ عَلَيْكَ وَالنِّسَاءُ سِوَاهَا كَثِيرٌ، وَسَلِ الْجَارِيَةَ تَصْدُقْكَ‏.‏ فَدَعَا رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم بَرِيرَةَ فَقَالَ ‏"‏ يَا بَرِيرَةُ هَلْ رَأَيْتِ فِيهَا شَيْئًا يَرِيبُكِ ‏"‏‏.‏ فَقَالَتْ بَرِيرَةُ لاَ وَالَّذِي بَعَثَكَ بِالْحَقِّ، إِنْ رَأَيْتُ مِنْهَا أَمْرًا أَغْمِصُهُ عَلَيْهَا أَكْثَرَ مِنْ أَنَّهَا جَارِيَةٌ حَدِيثَةُ السِّنِّ تَنَامُ عَنِ الْعَجِينَ فَتَأْتِي الدَّاجِنُ فَتَأْكُلُهُ‏.‏ فَقَامَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم مِنْ يَوْمِهِ، فَاسْتَعْذَرَ مِنْ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ أُبَىٍّ ابْنِ سَلُولَ فَقَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم ‏"‏ مَنْ يَعْذِرُنِي مِنْ رَجُلٍ بَلَغَنِي أَذَاهُ فِي أَهْلِي، فَوَاللَّهِ مَا عَلِمْتُ عَلَى أَهْلِي إِلاَّ خَيْرًا، وَقَدْ ذَكَرُوا رَجُلاً مَا عَلِمْتُ عَلَيْهِ إِلاَّ خَيْرًا، وَمَا كَانَ يَدْخُلُ عَلَى أَهْلِي إِلاَّ مَعِي ‏"‏‏.‏ فَقَامَ سَعْدُ بْنُ مُعَاذٍ فَقَالَ يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ أَنَا وَاللَّهِ أَعْذِرُكَ مِنْهُ، إِنْ كَانَ مِنَ الأَوْسِ ضَرَبْنَا عُنُقَهُ، وَإِنْ كَانَ مِنْ إِخْوَانِنَا مِنَ الْخَزْرَجِ أَمَرْتَنَا فَفَعَلْنَا فِيهِ أَمْرَكَ‏.‏ فَقَامَ سَعْدُ بْنُ عُبَادَةَ وَهُوَ سَيِّدُ الْخَزْرَجِ، وَكَانَ قَبْلَ ذَلِكَ رَجُلاً صَالِحًا وَلَكِنِ احْتَمَلَتْهُ الْحَمِيَّةُ فَقَالَ كَذَبْتَ لَعَمْرُ اللَّهِ، لاَ تَقْتُلُهُ وَلاَ تَقْدِرُ عَلَى ذَلِكَ، فَقَامَ أُسَيْدُ بْنُ الْحُضَيْرِ فَقَالَ كَذَبْتَ لَعَمْرُ اللَّهِ، وَاللَّهِ لَنَقْتُلَنَّهُ، فَإِنَّكَ مُنَافِقٌ تُجَادِلُ عَنِ الْمُنَافِقِينَ‏.‏ فَثَارَ الْحَيَّانِ الأَوْسُ وَالْخَزْرَجُ حَتَّى هَمُّوا، وَرَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم عَلَى الْمِنْبَرِ فَنَزَلَ فَخَفَّضَهُمْ حَتَّى سَكَتُوا وَسَكَتَ، وَبَكَيْتُ يَوْمِي لاَ يَرْقَأُ لِي دَمْعٌ وَلاَ أَكْتَحِلُ بِنَوْمٍ، فَأَصْبَحَ عِنْدِي أَبَوَاىَ، قَدْ بَكَيْتُ لَيْلَتَيْنِ وَيَوْمًا حَتَّى أَظُنُّ أَنَّ الْبُكَاءَ فَالِقٌ كَبِدِي ـ قَالَتْ ـ فَبَيْنَا هُمَا جَالِسَانِ عِنْدِي وَأَنَا أَبْكِي إِذِ اسْتَأْذَنَتِ امْرَأَةٌ مِنَ الأَنْصَارِ فَأَذِنْتُ لَهَا، فَجَلَسَتْ تَبْكِي مَعِي، فَبَيْنَا نَحْنُ كَذَلِكَ إِذْ دَخَلَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم فَجَلَسَ، وَلَمْ يَجْلِسْ عِنْدِي مِنْ يَوْمِ قِيلَ فِيَّ مَا قِيلَ قَبْلَهَا، وَقَدْ مَكُثَ شَهْرًا لاَ يُوحَى إِلَيْهِ فِي شَأْنِي شَىْءٌ ـ قَالَتْ ـ فَتَشَهَّدَ ثُمَّ قَالَ ‏"‏ يَا عَائِشَةُ فَإِنَّهُ بَلَغَنِي عَنْكِ كَذَا وَكَذَا، فَإِنْ كُنْتِ بَرِيئَةً فَسَيُبَرِّئُكِ اللَّهُ، وَإِنْ كُنْتِ أَلْمَمْتِ فَاسْتَغْفِرِي اللَّهَ وَتُوبِي إِلَيْهِ، فَإِنَّ الْعَبْدَ إِذَا اعْتَرَفَ بِذَنْبِهِ ثُمَّ تَابَ تَابَ اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ ‏"‏‏.‏ فَلَمَّا قَضَى رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم مَقَالَتَهُ قَلَصَ دَمْعِي حَتَّى مَا أُحِسُّ مِنْهُ قَطْرَةً وَقُلْتُ لأَبِي أَجِبْ عَنِّي رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم‏.‏ قَالَ وَاللَّهِ مَا أَدْرِي مَا أَقُولُ لِرَسُولِ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم‏.‏ فَقُلْتُ لأُمِّي أَجِيبِي عَنِّي رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم فِيمَا قَالَ‏.‏ قَالَتْ وَاللَّهِ مَا أَدْرِي مَا أَقُولُ لِرَسُولِ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم‏.‏ قَالَتْ وَأَنَا جَارِيَةٌ حَدِيثَةُ السِّنِّ لاَ أَقْرَأُ كَثِيرًا مِنَ الْقُرْآنِ فَقُلْتُ إِنِّي وَاللَّهِ لَقَدْ عَلِمْتُ أَنَّكُمْ سَمِعْتُمْ مَا يَتَحَدَّثُ بِهِ النَّاسُ، وَوَقَرَ فِي أَنْفُسِكُمْ وَصَدَّقْتُمْ بِهِ، وَلَئِنْ قُلْتُ لَكُمْ إِنِّي بَرِيئَةٌ‏.‏ وَاللَّهُ يَعْلَمُ إِنِّي لَبَرِيئَةٌ لاَ تُصَدِّقُونِي بِذَلِكَ، وَلَئِنِ اعْتَرَفْتُ لَكُمْ بِأَمْرٍ، وَاللَّهُ يَعْلَمُ أَنِّي بَرِيئَةٌ لَتُصَدِّقُنِّي وَاللَّهِ مَا أَجِدُ لِي وَلَكُمْ مَثَلاً إِلاَّ أَبَا يُوسُفَ إِذْ قَالَ ‏[quran sura="12" aya_start="18" aya_end="18"]{‏فَصَبْرٌ جَمِيلٌ وَاللَّهُ الْمُسْتَعَانُ عَلَى مَا تَصِفُونَ‏}‏ ثُمَّ تَحَوَّلْتُ عَلَى فِرَاشِي، وَأَنَا أَرْجُو أَنْ يُبَرِّئَنِي اللَّهُ، وَلَكِنْ وَاللَّهِ مَا ظَنَنْتُ أَنْ يُنْزِلَ فِي شَأْنِي وَحْيًا، وَلأَنَا أَحْقَرُ فِي نَفْسِي مِنْ أَنْ يُتَكَلَّمَ بِالْقُرْآنِ فِي أَمْرِي، وَلَكِنِّي كُنْتُ أَرْجُو أَنْ يَرَى رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم فِي النَّوْمِ رُؤْيَا يُبَرِّئُنِي اللَّهُ، فَوَاللَّهِ مَا رَامَ مَجْلِسَهُ وَلاَ خَرَجَ أَحَدٌ مِنْ أَهْلِ الْبَيْتِ حَتَّى أُنْزِلَ عَلَيْهِ، فَأَخَذَهُ مَا كَانَ يَأْخُذُهُ مِنَ الْبُرَحَاءِ، حَتَّى إِنَّهُ لَيَتَحَدَّرُ مِنْهُ مِثْلُ الْجُمَانِ مِنَ الْعَرَقِ فِي يَوْمٍ شَاتٍ، فَلَمَّا سُرِّيَ عَنْ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم وَهُوَ يَضْحَكُ، فَكَانَ أَوَّلَ كَلِمَةٍ تَكَلَّمَ بِهَا أَنْ قَالَ لِي ‏"‏ يَا عَائِشَةُ، احْمَدِي اللَّهَ فَقَدْ بَرَّأَكِ اللَّهُ ‏"‏‏.‏ فَقَالَتْ لِي أُمِّي قُومِي إِلَى رَسُولِ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم‏.‏ فَقُلْتُ لاَ وَاللَّهِ، لاَ أَقُومُ إِلَيْهِ، وَلاَ أَحْمَدُ إِلاَّ اللَّهَ فَأَنْزَلَ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى ‏[quran sura="24" aya_start="11" aya_end="11"]{‏إِنَّ الَّذِينَ جَاءُوا بِالإِفْكِ عُصْبَةٌ مِنْكُمْ‏}‏ الآيَاتِ، فَلَمَّا أَنْزَلَ اللَّهُ هَذَا فِي بَرَاءَتِي قَالَ أَبُو بَكْرٍ الصِّدِّيقُ ـ رضى الله عنه ـ وَكَانَ يُنْفِقُ عَلَى مِسْطَحِ بْنِ أُثَاثَةَ لِقَرَابَتِهِ مِنْهُ وَاللَّهِ لاَ أُنْفِقُ عَلَى مِسْطَحٍ شَيْئًا أَبَدًا بَعْدَ مَا قَالَ لِعَائِشَةَ‏.‏ فَأَنْزَلَ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى [quran sura="24" aya_start="22" aya_end="22"]‏{‏وَلاَ يَأْتَلِ أُولُو الْفَضْلِ مِنْكُمْ وَالسَّعَةِ‏}‏ إِلَى قَوْلِهِ [quran sura="24" aya_start="22" aya_end="22"]‏{‏غَفُورٌ رَحِيمٌ‏}‏ فَقَالَ أَبُو بَكْرٍ بَلَى، وَاللَّهِ إِنِّي لأُحِبُّ أَنْ يَغْفِرَ اللَّهُ لِي، فَرَجَعَ إِلَى مِسْطَحٍ الَّذِي كَانَ يُجْرِي عَلَيْهِ‏.‏ وَكَانَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم يَسْأَلُ زَيْنَبَ بِنْتَ جَحْشٍ عَنْ أَمْرِي، فَقَالَ ‏"‏ يَا زَيْنَبُ، مَا عَلِمْتِ مَا رَأَيْتِ ‏"‏‏.‏ فَقَالَتْ يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ، أَحْمِي سَمْعِي وَبَصَرِي، وَاللَّهِ مَا عَلِمْتُ عَلَيْهَا إِلاَّ خَيْرًا، قَالَتْ وَهْىَ الَّتِي كَانَتْ تُسَامِينِي، فَعَصَمَهَا اللَّهُ بِالْوَرَعِ‏.‏ قَالَ وَحَدَّثَنَا فُلَيْحٌ، عَنْ هِشَامِ بْنِ عُرْوَةَ، عَنْ عُرْوَةَ، عَنْ عَائِشَةَ، وَعَبْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ الزُّبَيْرِ، مِثْلَهُ‏.‏ قَالَ وَحَدَّثَنَا فُلَيْحٌ، عَنْ رَبِيعَةَ بْنِ أَبِي عَبْدِ الرَّحْمَنِ، وَيَحْيَى بْنِ سَعِيدٍ، عَنِ الْقَاسِمِ بْنِ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ أَبِي بَكْرٍ، مِثْلَهُ‏.‏
en_text: Abu al-Rabi‘ Sulayman ibn Dawud narrated to us, and Ahmad explained some of it to me. Fulayh ibn Sulayman narrated to us, from Ibn Shihab al-Zuhri, from ‘Urwah ibn al-Zubayr, Sa‘id ibn al-Musayyab, ‘Alqamah ibn Waqqas al-Laythi, and ‘Ubayd Allah ibn ‘Abd Allah ibn ‘Utbah, from ‘Aishah, may Allah be pleased with her, the wife of the Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, concerning what the people of the slander said about her, and how Allah declared her innocent of it. Al-Zuhri said: Each of them told me part of her account. Some had retained more of it than others and had remembered it more firmly. I have retained from each of them the report he narrated to me from ‘Aishah, and some parts of their reports confirm others. They said that ‘Aishah said: Whenever the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, intended to travel, he drew lots among his wives. Whichever one's lot came out, he would take her with him. On one expedition he undertook, he drew lots among us, and my lot came out. I went with him after the verse about the veil had been revealed. I was carried in a howdah and put down in it. We travelled until the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, had finished that expedition and was returning. When we had drawn near to Madinah, he announced one night that we would set off. I got up when they announced the departure and walked past the army. When I had finished what I needed to do, I came back to the riding place and felt my chest. My necklace, made of beads from the shells of Zafar, had broken. I went back to look for it, and searching for it delayed me. The men who used to prepare my mount came and lifted my howdah, placed it on the camel I rode, and set it off, thinking that I was inside it. At that time women were light in weight; they had not grown heavy or been covered with flesh. They ate only a little food. So when the men lifted the howdah and carried it away, they did not notice any unusual weight. I was a young girl. They sent the camel on and continued. I found my necklace after the army had moved on. I came to their stopping place, but no one was there. I went to the place where I had been staying and thought that they would notice I was missing and come back for me. While I was sitting there, sleep overcame me and I fell asleep. Safwan ibn al-Mu‘attal al-Sulami, then al-Dhakwani, had been behind the army. In the morning he reached the place where I was and saw the dark outline of a sleeping person. He came to me. He had seen me before the veil was prescribed. I woke when he said, ‘We belong to Allah, and to Him we return,’ as he made his camel kneel. He put its foreleg down, and I mounted it. He then led the camel with me until we reached the army after they had stopped to rest in the heat of midday. Some people were ruined, and the one who took the leading part in the slander was ‘Abd Allah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul. We arrived in Madinah, where I became ill for a month. During that time the people were repeating what the slanderers had said. What troubled me during my illness was that I did not see from the Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, the kindness I used to see from him when I was ill. He would only come in, greet me, and say, ‘How is that one?’ I did not know anything about the matter until I had recovered. Then I went out with Umm Mistah toward al-Manasi‘, the place where we relieved ourselves. We used to go out only from one night to the next. This was before we had built nearby latrines, and our practice was like that of the early Arabs in the open country or when travelling. Umm Mistah bint Abi Ruhm and I were walking when she stumbled over her cloak and said, ‘May Mistah be ruined!’ I said to her, ‘What a bad thing to say! Are you insulting a man who was present at Badr?’ She said, ‘You poor woman, have you not heard what they are saying?’ Then she told me what the slanderers were saying. My illness grew worse because of it. When I returned home, the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, came in, greeted me, and said, ‘How is that one?’ I said, ‘Will you let me go to my parents?’ I wanted to make sure of the report from them. The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, gave me permission, and I went to my parents. I said to my mother, ‘What are people talking about?’ She said, ‘My daughter, take it lightly. By Allah, it is rare for a beautiful woman who is loved by a man and has co-wives not to have them speak against her.’ I said, ‘Glory be to Allah! Are people really talking about this?’ I spent that night until morning with tears that would not stop and without sleeping. In the morning, when the revelation had been delayed, the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, called ‘Ali ibn Abi Talib and Usamah ibn Zayd to consult them about separating from his wife. Usamah advised him according to the affection he knew the Prophet had for his family. Usamah said, ‘They are your family, Messenger of Allah, and by Allah, we know nothing about them except good.’ ‘Ali ibn Abi Talib said, ‘Messenger of Allah, Allah has not placed any restriction on you; there are many women besides her. Ask the servant girl and she will tell you the truth.’ The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, called for Barirah and said, ‘Barirah, have you seen anything about her that makes you doubt her?’ Barirah said, ‘No, by the One who sent you with the truth. I have seen nothing in her that I could criticize, except that she is a young girl who sometimes falls asleep while the dough is rising, and then the household animal comes and eats it.’ That day the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, stood up and sought support against ‘Abd Allah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul. He said, ‘Who will help me against a man whose harm to my family has reached me? By Allah, I know nothing about my family except good. They have also mentioned a man about whom I know nothing except good, and he never entered my family’s home except when he was with me.’ Sa‘d ibn Mu‘adh stood up and said, ‘Messenger of Allah, by Allah, I will help you against him. If he is from the Aws, we will strike his neck, and if he is one of our brothers from the Khazraj, command us and we will carry out your command against him.’ Sa‘d ibn ‘Ubadah, the chief of the Khazraj, then stood up. He had previously been a righteous man, but anger overcame him. He said, ‘By the life of Allah, you have lied. You will not kill him, and you are not able to do that.’ Usayd ibn Hudayr stood up and said, ‘By the life of Allah, you have lied. By Allah, we will kill him, for you are a hypocrite arguing on behalf of the hypocrites.’ The two clans, Aws and Khazraj, became stirred up until they were about to fight, while the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, was standing on the pulpit. He came down and calmed them until they fell silent, and then he was silent. I cried that whole day, with tears that would not stop, and without sleeping. The next morning my parents were with me. I had cried for two nights and a day, until I thought that the crying would split my liver. While they were sitting with me and I was crying, a woman from the Ansar asked permission to come in. I let her in, and she sat and cried with me. While we were like that, the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, came in and sat down. He had not sat with me since the day people had said what they said about me. A month had passed without any revelation being sent to him concerning me. He began by bearing witness, then said, ‘Aishah, I have heard such-and-such about you. If you are innocent, Allah will declare you innocent. If you have committed a sin, then ask Allah for forgiveness and repent to Him, for when a servant admits a sin and then repents, Allah accepts his repentance.’ When the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, had finished speaking, my tears dried up until I could no longer feel a single drop. I said to my father, ‘Answer the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, on my behalf.’ He said, ‘By Allah, I do not know what to say to the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him.’ I said to my mother, ‘Answer the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, on my behalf about what he said.’ She said, ‘By Allah, I do not know what to say to the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him.’ I was a young girl and did not recite much of the Quran. I said, ‘By Allah, I know that you have heard what people are saying, and it has settled in your hearts and you have believed it. If I tell you that I am innocent—and Allah knows that I am innocent—you will not believe me. But if I admit something to you, while Allah knows that I am innocent, you will believe me. By Allah, I can find no example for you and me except the father of Yusuf, who said, “So patience is most fitting, and Allah is the One whose help is sought against what you describe” (12:18).’ Then I turned over on my bed, hoping that Allah would declare me innocent. But by Allah, I did not think that revelation would be sent down concerning me. I considered myself too insignificant for Quran to be revealed about my matter. I had only hoped that the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, would see a dream in which Allah declared me innocent. By Allah, he had not left his seat, and no one from the household had gone out, when revelation came down to him. He was overcome by the state that used to come over him, until sweat like pearls ran down from him on a cold day. When that state passed from the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, he was smiling. The first words he said to me were, ‘Aishah, praise Allah, for Allah has declared you innocent.’ My mother said to me, ‘Get up and go to the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him.’ I said, ‘No, by Allah, I will not get up to go to him, and I will praise none but Allah.’ Then Allah Most High revealed, ‘Indeed, those who brought the slander are a group among you’ and the verses that follow (24:11). When Allah revealed this declaring me innocent, Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, may Allah be pleased with him, who used to support Mistah ibn Uthathah because of their kinship, said, ‘By Allah, I will never spend anything on Mistah again after what he said about Aishah.’ Then Allah Most High revealed, ‘Those of you who possess grace and abundance should not swear…’ up to His words, ‘…All-Forgiving, Most Merciful’ (24:22). Abu Bakr said, ‘Indeed, by Allah, I love that Allah should forgive me.’ So he returned to supporting Mistah as he had done before. The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, also asked Zaynab bint Jahsh about me. He said, ‘Zaynab, what have you known or seen?’ She replied, ‘Messenger of Allah, I protect my hearing and my sight. By Allah, I know nothing about her except good.’ ‘Aishah said: She was the one who used to compete with me for the Prophet’s favor, but Allah protected her through her piety. He said: Fulayh narrated to us from Hisham ibn ‘Urwah, from ‘Urwah, from ‘Aishah and ‘Abd Allah ibn al-Zubayr, the same report. He said: Fulayh narrated to us from Rabi‘ah ibn Abi ‘Abd al-Rahman and Yahya ibn Sa‘id, from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Bakr, the same report.

reference: Sahih al-Bukhari, hadith 2731, 2732, book 54, باب الشُّرُوطِ فِي الْجِهَادِ وَالْمُصَالَحَةِ مَعَ أَهْلِ الْحَرْبِ وَكِتَابَةِ الشُّرُوطِ
text_original: حَدَّثَنِي عَبْدُ اللَّهِ بْنُ مُحَمَّدٍ، حَدَّثَنَا عَبْدُ الرَّزَّاقِ، أَخْبَرَنَا مَعْمَرٌ، قَالَ أَخْبَرَنِي الزُّهْرِيُّ، قَالَ أَخْبَرَنِي عُرْوَةُ بْنُ الزُّبَيْرِ، عَنِ الْمِسْوَرِ بْنِ مَخْرَمَةَ، وَمَرْوَانَ، يُصَدِّقُ كُلُّ وَاحِدٍ مِنْهُمَا حَدِيثَ صَاحِبِهِ قَالَ خَرَجَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم زَمَنَ الْحُدَيْبِيَةِ، حَتَّى كَانُوا بِبَعْضِ الطَّرِيقِ قَالَ النَّبِيُّ صلى الله عليه وسلم ‏"‏ إِنَّ خَالِدَ بْنَ الْوَلِيدِ بِالْغَمِيمِ فِي خَيْلٍ لِقُرَيْشٍ طَلِيعَةً فَخُذُوا ذَاتَ الْيَمِينِ ‏"‏‏.‏ فَوَاللَّهِ مَا شَعَرَ بِهِمْ خَالِدٌ حَتَّى إِذَا هُمْ بِقَتَرَةِ الْجَيْشِ، فَانْطَلَقَ يَرْكُضُ نَذِيرًا لِقُرَيْشٍ، وَسَارَ النَّبِيُّ صلى الله عليه وسلم حَتَّى إِذَا كَانَ بِالثَّنِيَّةِ الَّتِي يُهْبَطُ عَلَيْهِمْ مِنْهَا، بَرَكَتْ بِهِ رَاحِلَتُهُ‏.‏ فَقَالَ النَّاسُ حَلْ حَلْ‏.‏ فَأَلَحَّتْ، فَقَالُوا خَلأَتِ الْقَصْوَاءُ، خَلأَتِ الْقَصْوَاءُ‏.‏ فَقَالَ النَّبِيُّ صلى الله عليه وسلم ‏"‏ مَا خَلأَتِ الْقَصْوَاءُ، وَمَا ذَاكَ لَهَا بِخُلُقٍ، وَلَكِنْ حَبَسَهَا حَابِسُ الْفِيلِ، ثُمَّ قَالَ وَالَّذِي نَفْسِي بِيَدِهِ لاَ يَسْأَلُونِي خُطَّةً يُعَظِّمُونَ فِيهَا حُرُمَاتِ اللَّهِ إِلاَّ أَعْطَيْتُهُمْ إِيَّاهَا ‏"‏‏.‏ ثُمَّ زَجَرَهَا فَوَثَبَتْ، قَالَ فَعَدَلَ عَنْهُمْ حَتَّى نَزَلَ بِأَقْصَى الْحُدَيْبِيَةِ، عَلَى ثَمَدٍ قَلِيلِ الْمَاءِ يَتَبَرَّضُهُ النَّاسُ تَبَرُّضًا، فَلَمْ يُلَبِّثْهُ النَّاسُ حَتَّى نَزَحُوهُ، وَشُكِيَ إِلَى رَسُولِ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم الْعَطَشُ، فَانْتَزَعَ سَهْمًا مِنْ كِنَانَتِهِ، ثُمَّ أَمَرَهُمْ أَنْ يَجْعَلُوهُ فِيهِ، فَوَاللَّهِ مَا زَالَ يَجِيشُ لَهُمْ بِالرِّيِّ حَتَّى صَدَرُوا عَنْهُ، فَبَيْنَمَا هُمْ كَذَلِكَ، إِذْ جَاءَ بُدَيْلُ بْنُ وَرْقَاءَ الْخُزَاعِيُّ فِي نَفَرٍ مِنْ قَوْمِهِ مِنْ خُزَاعَةَ، وَكَانُوا عَيْبَةَ نُصْحِ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم مِنْ أَهْلِ تِهَامَةَ، فَقَالَ إِنِّي تَرَكْتُ كَعْبَ بْنَ لُؤَىٍّ وَعَامِرَ بْنَ لُؤَىٍّ نَزَلُوا أَعْدَادَ مِيَاهِ الْحُدَيْبِيَةِ، وَمَعَهُمُ الْعُوذُ الْمَطَافِيلُ، وَهُمْ مُقَاتِلُوكَ وَصَادُّوكَ عَنِ الْبَيْتِ‏.‏ فَقَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم ‏"‏ إِنَّا لَمْ نَجِئْ لِقِتَالِ أَحَدٍ، وَلَكِنَّا جِئْنَا مُعْتَمِرِينَ، وَإِنَّ قُرَيْشًا قَدْ نَهِكَتْهُمُ الْحَرْبُ، وَأَضَرَّتْ بِهِمْ، فَإِنْ شَاءُوا مَادَدْتُهُمْ مُدَّةً، وَيُخَلُّوا بَيْنِي وَبَيْنَ النَّاسِ، فَإِنْ أَظْهَرْ فَإِنْ شَاءُوا أَنْ يَدْخُلُوا فِيمَا دَخَلَ فِيهِ النَّاسُ فَعَلُوا، وَإِلاَّ فَقَدْ جَمُّوا، وَإِنْ هُمْ أَبَوْا فَوَالَّذِي نَفْسِي بِيَدِهِ، لأُقَاتِلَنَّهُمْ عَلَى أَمْرِي هَذَا حَتَّى تَنْفَرِدَ سَالِفَتِي، وَلَيُنْفِذَنَّ اللَّهُ أَمْرَهُ ‏"‏‏.‏ فَقَالَ بُدَيْلٌ سَأُبَلِّغُهُمْ مَا تَقُولُ‏.‏ قَالَ فَانْطَلَقَ حَتَّى أَتَى قُرَيْشًا قَالَ إِنَّا قَدْ جِئْنَاكُمْ مِنْ هَذَا الرَّجُلِ، وَسَمِعْنَاهُ يَقُولُ قَوْلاً، فَإِنْ شِئْتُمْ أَنْ نَعْرِضَهُ عَلَيْكُمْ فَعَلْنَا، فَقَالَ سُفَهَاؤُهُمْ لاَ حَاجَةَ لَنَا أَنْ تُخْبِرَنَا عَنْهُ بِشَىْءٍ‏.‏ وَقَالَ ذَوُو الرَّأْىِ مِنْهُمْ هَاتِ مَا سَمِعْتَهُ يَقُولُ‏.‏ قَالَ سَمِعْتُهُ يَقُولُ كَذَا وَكَذَا، فَحَدَّثَهُمْ بِمَا قَالَ النَّبِيُّ صلى الله عليه وسلم‏.‏ فَقَامَ عُرْوَةُ بْنُ مَسْعُودٍ فَقَالَ أَىْ قَوْمِ أَلَسْتُمْ بِالْوَالِدِ قَالُوا بَلَى‏.‏ قَالَ أَوَلَسْتُ بِالْوَلَدِ قَالُوا بَلَى‏.‏ قَالَ فَهَلْ تَتَّهِمُونِي‏.‏ قَالُوا لاَ‏.‏ قَالَ أَلَسْتُمْ تَعْلَمُونَ أَنِّي اسْتَنْفَرْتُ أَهْلَ عُكَاظٍ، فَلَمَّا بَلَّحُوا عَلَىَّ جِئْتُكُمْ بِأَهْلِي وَوَلَدِي وَمَنْ أَطَاعَنِي قَالُوا بَلَى‏.‏ قَالَ فَإِنَّ هَذَا قَدْ عَرَضَ لَكُمْ خُطَّةَ رُشْدٍ، اقْبَلُوهَا وَدَعُونِي آتِهِ‏.‏ قَالُوا ائْتِهِ‏.‏ فَأَتَاهُ فَجَعَلَ يُكَلِّمُ النَّبِيَّ صلى الله عليه وسلم فَقَالَ النَّبِيُّ صلى الله عليه وسلم نَحْوًا مِنْ قَوْلِهِ لِبُدَيْلٍ، فَقَالَ عُرْوَةُ عِنْدَ ذَلِكَ أَىْ مُحَمَّدُ، أَرَأَيْتَ إِنِ اسْتَأْصَلْتَ أَمْرَ قَوْمِكَ هَلْ سَمِعْتَ بِأَحَدٍ مِنَ الْعَرَبِ اجْتَاحَ أَهْلَهُ قَبْلَكَ وَإِنْ تَكُنِ الأُخْرَى، فَإِنِّي وَاللَّهِ لأَرَى وُجُوهًا، وَإِنِّي لأَرَى أَوْشَابًا مِنَ النَّاسِ خَلِيقًا أَنْ يَفِرُّوا وَيَدَعُوكَ‏.‏ فَقَالَ لَهُ أَبُو بَكْرٍ امْصُصْ بَظْرَ اللاَّتِ، أَنَحْنُ نَفِرُّ عَنْهُ وَنَدَعُهُ فَقَالَ مَنْ ذَا قَالُوا أَبُو بَكْرٍ‏.‏ قَالَ أَمَا وَالَّذِي نَفْسِي بِيَدِهِ لَوْلاَ يَدٌ كَانَتْ لَكَ عِنْدِي لَمْ أَجْزِكَ بِهَا لأَجَبْتُكَ‏.‏ قَالَ وَجَعَلَ يُكَلِّمُ النَّبِيَّ صلى الله عليه وسلم فَكُلَّمَا تَكَلَّمَ أَخَذَ بِلِحْيَتِهِ، وَالْمُغِيرَةُ بْنُ شُعْبَةَ قَائِمٌ عَلَى رَأْسِ النَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه وسلم وَمَعَهُ السَّيْفُ وَعَلَيْهِ الْمِغْفَرُ، فَكُلَّمَا أَهْوَى عُرْوَةُ بِيَدِهِ إِلَى لِحْيَةِ النَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه وسلم ضَرَبَ يَدَهُ بِنَعْلِ السَّيْفِ، وَقَالَ لَهُ أَخِّرْ يَدَكَ عَنْ لِحْيَةِ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم‏.‏ فَرَفَعَ عُرْوَةُ رَأْسَهُ فَقَالَ مَنْ هَذَا قَالُوا الْمُغِيرَةُ بْنُ شُعْبَةَ‏.‏ فَقَالَ أَىْ غُدَرُ، أَلَسْتُ أَسْعَى فِي غَدْرَتِكَ وَكَانَ الْمُغِيرَةُ صَحِبَ قَوْمًا فِي الْجَاهِلِيَّةِ، فَقَتَلَهُمْ، وَأَخَذَ أَمْوَالَهُمْ، ثُمَّ جَاءَ فَأَسْلَمَ فَقَالَ النَّبِيُّ صلى الله عليه وسلم ‏"‏ أَمَّا الإِسْلاَمَ فَأَقْبَلُ، وَأَمَّا الْمَالَ فَلَسْتُ مِنْهُ فِي شَىْءٍ ‏"‏‏.‏ ثُمَّ إِنَّ عُرْوَةَ جَعَلَ يَرْمُقُ أَصْحَابَ النَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه وسلم بِعَيْنَيْهِ‏.‏ قَالَ فَوَاللَّهِ مَا تَنَخَّمَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم نُخَامَةً إِلاَّ وَقَعَتْ فِي كَفِّ رَجُلٍ مِنْهُمْ فَدَلَكَ بِهَا وَجْهَهُ وَجِلْدَهُ، وَإِذَا أَمَرَهُمُ ابْتَدَرُوا أَمْرَهُ، وَإِذَا تَوَضَّأَ كَادُوا يَقْتَتِلُونَ عَلَى وَضُوئِهِ، وَإِذَا تَكَلَّمَ خَفَضُوا أَصْوَاتَهُمْ عِنْدَهُ، وَمَا يُحِدُّونَ إِلَيْهِ النَّظَرَ تَعْظِيمًا لَهُ، فَرَجَعَ عُرْوَةُ إِلَى أَصْحَابِهِ، فَقَالَ أَىْ قَوْمِ، وَاللَّهِ لَقَدْ وَفَدْتُ عَلَى الْمُلُوكِ، وَوَفَدْتُ عَلَى قَيْصَرَ وَكِسْرَى وَالنَّجَاشِيِّ وَاللَّهِ إِنْ رَأَيْتُ مَلِكًا قَطُّ، يُعَظِّمُهُ أَصْحَابُهُ مَا يُعَظِّمُ أَصْحَابُ مُحَمَّدٍ صلى الله عليه وسلم مُحَمَّدًا، وَاللَّهِ إِنْ تَنَخَّمَ نُخَامَةً إِلاَّ وَقَعَتْ فِي كَفِّ رَجُلٍ مِنْهُمْ، فَدَلَكَ بِهَا وَجْهَهُ وَجِلْدَهُ، وَإِذَا أَمَرَهُمُ ابْتَدَرُوا أَمْرَهُ وَإِذَا تَوَضَّأَ كَادُوا يَقْتَتِلُونَ عَلَى وَضُوئِهِ، وَإِذَا تَكَلَّمَ خَفَضُوا أَصْوَاتَهُمْ عِنْدَهُ، وَمَا يُحِدُّونَ إِلَيْهِ النَّظَرَ تَعْظِيمًا لَهُ، وَإِنَّهُ قَدْ عَرَضَ عَلَيْكُمْ خُطَّةَ رُشْدٍ، فَاقْبَلُوهَا‏.‏ فَقَالَ رَجُلٌ مِنْ بَنِي كِنَانَةَ دَعُونِي آتِهِ‏.‏ فَقَالُوا ائْتِهِ‏.‏ فَلَمَّا أَشْرَفَ عَلَى النَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه وسلم وَأَصْحَابِهِ، قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم ‏"‏ هَذَا فُلاَنٌ، وَهْوَ مِنْ قَوْمٍ يُعَظِّمُونَ الْبُدْنَ فَابْعَثُوهَا لَهُ ‏"‏‏.‏ فَبُعِثَتْ لَهُ وَاسْتَقْبَلَهُ النَّاسُ يُلَبُّونَ، فَلَمَّا رَأَى ذَلِكَ قَالَ سُبْحَانَ اللَّهِ مَا يَنْبَغِي لِهَؤُلاَءِ أَنْ يُصَدُّوا عَنِ الْبَيْتِ، فَلَمَّا رَجَعَ إِلَى أَصْحَابِهِ قَالَ رَأَيْتُ الْبُدْنَ قَدْ قُلِّدَتْ وَأُشْعِرَتْ، فَمَا أَرَى أَنْ يُصَدُّوا عَنِ الْبَيْتِ‏.‏ فَقَامَ رَجُلٌ مِنْهُمْ يُقَالُ لَهُ مِكْرَزُ بْنُ حَفْصٍ‏.‏ فَقَالَ دَعُونِي آتِهِ‏.‏ فَقَالُوا ائْتِهِ‏.‏ فَلَمَّا أَشْرَفَ عَلَيْهِمْ قَالَ النَّبِيُّ صلى الله عليه وسلم ‏"‏ هَذَا مِكْرَزٌ وَهْوَ رَجُلٌ فَاجِرٌ ‏"‏‏.‏ فَجَعَلَ يُكَلِّمُ النَّبِيَّ صلى الله عليه وسلم، فَبَيْنَمَا هُوَ يُكَلِّمُهُ إِذْ جَاءَ سُهَيْلُ بْنُ عَمْرٍو‏.‏ قَالَ مَعْمَرٌ فَأَخْبَرَنِي أَيُّوبُ عَنْ عِكْرِمَةَ، أَنَّهُ لَمَّا جَاءَ سُهَيْلُ بْنُ عَمْرٍو قَالَ النَّبِيُّ صلى الله عليه وسلم ‏"‏ لَقَدْ سَهُلَ لَكُمْ مِنْ أَمْرِكُمْ ‏"‏‏.‏ قَالَ مَعْمَرٌ قَالَ الزُّهْرِيُّ فِي حَدِيثِهِ فَجَاءَ سُهَيْلُ بْنُ عَمْرٍو فَقَالَ هَاتِ، اكْتُبْ بَيْنَنَا وَبَيْنَكُمْ كِتَابًا، فَدَعَا النَّبِيُّ صلى الله عليه وسلم الْكَاتِبَ، فَقَالَ النَّبِيُّ صلى الله عليه وسلم ‏"‏ بِسْمِ اللَّهِ الرَّحْمَنِ الرَّحِيمِ ‏"‏‏.‏ قَالَ سُهَيْلٌ أَمَّا الرَّحْمَنُ فَوَاللَّهِ مَا أَدْرِي مَا هُوَ وَلَكِنِ اكْتُبْ بِاسْمِكَ اللَّهُمَّ‏.‏ كَمَا كُنْتَ تَكْتُبُ‏.‏ فَقَالَ الْمُسْلِمُونَ وَاللَّهِ لاَ نَكْتُبُهَا إِلاَّ بِسْمِ اللَّهِ الرَّحْمَنِ الرَّحِيمِ‏.‏ فَقَالَ النَّبِيُّ صلى الله عليه وسلم ‏"‏ اكْتُبْ بِاسْمِكَ اللَّهُمَّ ‏"‏‏.‏ ثُمَّ قَالَ ‏"‏ هَذَا مَا قَاضَى عَلَيْهِ مُحَمَّدٌ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ‏"‏‏.‏ فَقَالَ سُهَيْلٌ وَاللَّهِ لَوْ كُنَّا نَعْلَمُ أَنَّكَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ مَا صَدَدْنَاكَ عَنِ الْبَيْتِ وَلاَ قَاتَلْنَاكَ، وَلَكِنِ اكْتُبْ مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ‏.‏ فَقَالَ النَّبِيُّ صلى الله عليه وسلم ‏"‏ وَاللَّهِ إِنِّي لَرَسُولُ اللَّهِ وَإِنْ كَذَّبْتُمُونِي‏.‏ اكْتُبْ مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ‏"‏‏.‏ قَالَ الزُّهْرِيُّ وَذَلِكَ لِقَوْلِهِ ‏"‏ لاَ يَسْأَلُونِي خُطَّةً يُعَظِّمُونَ فِيهَا حُرُمَاتِ اللَّهِ إِلاَّ أَعْطَيْتُهُمْ إِيَّاهَا ‏"‏‏.‏ فَقَالَ لَهُ النَّبِيُّ صلى الله عليه وسلم ‏"‏ عَلَى أَنْ تُخَلُّوا بَيْنَنَا وَبَيْنَ الْبَيْتِ فَنَطُوفَ بِهِ ‏"‏‏.‏ فَقَالَ سُهَيْلٌ وَاللَّهِ لاَ تَتَحَدَّثُ الْعَرَبُ أَنَّا أُخِذْنَا ضُغْطَةً وَلَكِنْ ذَلِكَ مِنَ الْعَامِ الْمُقْبِلِ فَكَتَبَ‏.‏ فَقَالَ سُهَيْلٌ وَعَلَى أَنَّهُ لاَ يَأْتِيكَ مِنَّا رَجُلٌ، وَإِنْ كَانَ عَلَى دِينِكَ، إِلاَّ رَدَدْتَهُ إِلَيْنَا‏.‏ قَالَ الْمُسْلِمُونَ سُبْحَانَ اللَّهِ كَيْفَ يُرَدُّ إِلَى الْمُشْرِكِينَ وَقَدْ جَاءَ مُسْلِمًا فَبَيْنَمَا هُمْ كَذَلِكَ إِذْ دَخَلَ أَبُو جَنْدَلِ بْنُ سُهَيْلِ بْنِ عَمْرٍو يَرْسُفُ فِي قُيُودِهِ، وَقَدْ خَرَجَ مِنْ أَسْفَلِ مَكَّةَ، حَتَّى رَمَى بِنَفْسِهِ بَيْنَ أَظْهُرِ الْمُسْلِمِينَ‏.‏ فَقَالَ سُهَيْلٌ هَذَا يَا مُحَمَّدُ أَوَّلُ مَا أُقَاضِيكَ عَلَيْهِ أَنْ تَرُدَّهُ إِلَىَّ‏.‏ فَقَالَ النَّبِيُّ صلى الله عليه وسلم ‏"‏ إِنَّا لَمْ نَقْضِ الْكِتَابَ بَعْدُ ‏"‏‏.‏ قَالَ فَوَاللَّهِ إِذًا لَمْ أُصَالِحْكَ عَلَى شَىْءٍ أَبَدًا‏.‏ قَالَ النَّبِيُّ صلى الله عليه وسلم ‏"‏ فَأَجِزْهُ لِي ‏"‏‏.‏ قَالَ مَا أَنَا بِمُجِيزِهِ لَكَ‏.‏ قَالَ ‏"‏ بَلَى، فَافْعَلْ ‏"‏‏.‏ قَالَ مَا أَنَا بِفَاعِلٍ‏.‏ قَالَ مِكْرَزٌ بَلْ قَدْ أَجَزْنَاهُ لَكَ‏.‏ قَالَ أَبُو جَنْدَلٍ أَىْ مَعْشَرَ الْمُسْلِمِينَ، أُرَدُّ إِلَى الْمُشْرِكِينَ وَقَدْ جِئْتُ مُسْلِمًا أَلاَ تَرَوْنَ مَا قَدْ لَقِيتُ وَكَانَ قَدْ عُذِّبَ عَذَابًا شَدِيدًا فِي اللَّهِ‏.‏ قَالَ فَقَالَ عُمَرُ بْنُ الْخَطَّابِ فَأَتَيْتُ نَبِيَّ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم فَقُلْتُ أَلَسْتَ نَبِيَّ اللَّهِ حَقًّا قَالَ ‏"‏ بَلَى ‏"‏‏.‏ قُلْتُ أَلَسْنَا عَلَى الْحَقِّ وَعَدُوُّنَا عَلَى الْبَاطِلِ قَالَ ‏"‏ بَلَى ‏"‏‏.‏ قُلْتُ فَلِمَ نُعْطِي الدَّنِيَّةَ فِي دِينِنَا إِذًا قَالَ ‏"‏ إِنِّي رَسُولُ اللَّهِ، وَلَسْتُ أَعْصِيهِ وَهْوَ نَاصِرِي ‏"‏‏.‏ قُلْتُ أَوَلَيْسَ كُنْتَ تُحَدِّثُنَا أَنَّا سَنَأْتِي الْبَيْتَ فَنَطُوفُ بِهِ قَالَ ‏"‏ بَلَى، فَأَخْبَرْتُكَ أَنَّا نَأْتِيهِ الْعَامَ ‏"‏‏.‏ قَالَ قُلْتُ لاَ‏.‏ قَالَ ‏"‏ فَإِنَّكَ آتِيهِ وَمُطَّوِّفٌ بِهِ ‏"‏‏.‏ قَالَ فَأَتَيْتُ أَبَا بَكْرٍ فَقُلْتُ يَا أَبَا بَكْرٍ، أَلَيْسَ هَذَا نَبِيَّ اللَّهِ حَقًّا قَالَ بَلَى‏.‏ قُلْتُ أَلَسْنَا عَلَى الْحَقِّ وَعَدُوُّنَا عَلَى الْبَاطِلِ قَالَ بَلَى‏.‏ قُلْتُ فَلِمَ نُعْطِي الدَّنِيَّةَ فِي دِينِنَا إِذًا قَالَ أَيُّهَا الرَّجُلُ، إِنَّهُ لَرَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم وَلَيْسَ يَعْصِي رَبَّهُ وَهْوَ نَاصِرُهُ، فَاسْتَمْسِكْ بِغَرْزِهِ، فَوَاللَّهِ إِنَّهُ عَلَى الْحَقِّ‏.‏ قُلْتُ أَلَيْسَ كَانَ يُحَدِّثُنَا أَنَّا سَنَأْتِي الْبَيْتَ وَنَطُوفُ بِهِ قَالَ بَلَى، أَفَأَخْبَرَكَ أَنَّكَ تَأْتِيهِ الْعَامَ قُلْتُ لاَ‏.‏ قَالَ فَإِنَّكَ آتِيهِ وَمُطَّوِّفٌ بِهِ‏.‏ قَالَ الزُّهْرِيِّ قَالَ عُمَرُ فَعَمِلْتُ لِذَلِكَ أَعْمَالاً‏.‏ قَالَ فَلَمَّا فَرَغَ مِنْ قَضِيَّةِ الْكِتَابِ قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم لأَصْحَابِهِ ‏"‏ قُومُوا فَانْحَرُوا، ثُمَّ احْلِقُوا ‏"‏‏.‏ قَالَ فَوَاللَّهِ مَا قَامَ مِنْهُمْ رَجُلٌ حَتَّى قَالَ ذَلِكَ ثَلاَثَ مَرَّاتٍ، فَلَمَّا لَمْ يَقُمْ مِنْهُمْ أَحَدٌ دَخَلَ عَلَى أُمِّ سَلَمَةَ، فَذَكَرَ لَهَا مَا لَقِيَ مِنَ النَّاسِ‏.‏ فَقَالَتْ أُمُّ سَلَمَةَ يَا نَبِيَّ اللَّهِ، أَتُحِبُّ ذَلِكَ اخْرُجْ ثُمَّ لاَ تُكَلِّمْ أَحَدًا مِنْهُمْ كَلِمَةً حَتَّى تَنْحَرَ بُدْنَكَ، وَتَدْعُوَ حَالِقَكَ فَيَحْلِقَكَ‏.‏ فَخَرَجَ فَلَمْ يُكَلِّمْ أَحَدًا مِنْهُمْ، حَتَّى فَعَلَ ذَلِكَ نَحَرَ بُدْنَهُ، وَدَعَا حَالِقَهُ فَحَلَقَهُ‏.‏ فَلَمَّا رَأَوْا ذَلِكَ، قَامُوا فَنَحَرُوا، وَجَعَلَ بَعْضُهُمْ يَحْلِقُ بَعْضًا، حَتَّى كَادَ بَعْضُهُمْ يَقْتُلُ بَعْضًا غَمًّا، ثُمَّ جَاءَهُ نِسْوَةٌ مُؤْمِنَاتٌ فَأَنْزَلَ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى ‏[quran sura="60" aya_start="10" aya_end="10"]{‏يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا إِذَا جَاءَكُمُ الْمُؤْمِنَاتُ مُهَاجِرَاتٍ فَامْتَحِنُوهُنَّ‏}‏ حَتَّى بَلَغَ ‏[quran sura="60" aya_start="10" aya_end="10"]{‏بِعِصَمِ الْكَوَافِرِ‏}‏ فَطَلَّقَ عُمَرُ يَوْمَئِذٍ امْرَأَتَيْنِ كَانَتَا لَهُ فِي الشِّرْكِ، فَتَزَوَّجَ إِحْدَاهُمَا مُعَاوِيَةُ بْنُ أَبِي سُفْيَانَ، وَالأُخْرَى صَفْوَانُ بْنُ أُمَيَّةَ، ثُمَّ رَجَعَ النَّبِيُّ صلى الله عليه وسلم إِلَى الْمَدِينَةِ، فَجَاءَهُ أَبُو بَصِيرٍ ـ رَجُلٌ مِنْ قُرَيْشٍ ـ وَهْوَ مُسْلِمٌ فَأَرْسَلُوا فِي طَلَبِهِ رَجُلَيْنِ، فَقَالُوا الْعَهْدَ الَّذِي جَعَلْتَ لَنَا‏.‏ فَدَفَعَهُ إِلَى الرَّجُلَيْنِ، فَخَرَجَا بِهِ حَتَّى بَلَغَا ذَا الْحُلَيْفَةِ، فَنَزَلُوا يَأْكُلُونَ مِنْ تَمْرٍ لَهُمْ، فَقَالَ أَبُو بَصِيرٍ لأَحَدِ الرَّجُلَيْنِ وَاللَّهِ إِنِّي لأَرَى سَيْفَكَ هَذَا يَا فُلاَنُ جَيِّدًا‏.‏ فَاسْتَلَّهُ الآخَرُ فَقَالَ أَجَلْ، وَاللَّهِ إِنَّهُ لَجَيِّدٌ، لَقَدْ جَرَّبْتُ بِهِ ثُمَّ جَرَّبْتُ‏.‏ فَقَالَ أَبُو بَصِيرٍ أَرِنِي أَنْظُرْ إِلَيْهِ، فَأَمْكَنَهُ مِنْهُ، فَضَرَبَهُ حَتَّى بَرَدَ، وَفَرَّ الآخَرُ، حَتَّى أَتَى الْمَدِينَةَ، فَدَخَلَ الْمَسْجِدَ يَعْدُو‏.‏ فَقَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم حِينَ رَآهُ ‏"‏ لَقَدْ رَأَى هَذَا ذُعْرًا ‏"‏‏.‏ فَلَمَّا انْتَهَى إِلَى النَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه وسلم قَالَ قُتِلَ وَاللَّهِ صَاحِبِي وَإِنِّي لَمَقْتُولٌ، فَجَاءَ أَبُو بَصِيرٍ فَقَالَ يَا نَبِيَّ اللَّهِ، قَدْ وَاللَّهِ أَوْفَى اللَّهُ ذِمَّتَكَ، قَدْ رَدَدْتَنِي إِلَيْهِمْ ثُمَّ أَنْجَانِي اللَّهُ مِنْهُمْ‏.‏ قَالَ النَّبِيُّ صلى الله عليه وسلم ‏"‏ وَيْلُ أُمِّهِ مِسْعَرَ حَرْبٍ، لَوْ كَانَ لَهُ أَحَدٌ ‏"‏‏.‏ فَلَمَّا سَمِعَ ذَلِكَ عَرَفَ أَنَّهُ سَيَرُدُّهُ إِلَيْهِمْ، فَخَرَجَ حَتَّى أَتَى سِيفَ الْبَحْرِ‏.‏ قَالَ وَيَنْفَلِتُ مِنْهُمْ أَبُو جَنْدَلِ بْنُ سُهَيْلٍ، فَلَحِقَ بِأَبِي بَصِيرٍ، فَجَعَلَ لاَ يَخْرُجُ مِنْ قُرَيْشٍ رَجُلٌ قَدْ أَسْلَمَ إِلاَّ لَحِقَ بِأَبِي بَصِيرٍ، حَتَّى اجْتَمَعَتْ مِنْهُمْ عِصَابَةٌ، فَوَاللَّهِ مَا يَسْمَعُونَ بِعِيرٍ خَرَجَتْ لِقُرَيْشٍ إِلَى الشَّأْمِ إِلاَّ اعْتَرَضُوا لَهَا، فَقَتَلُوهُمْ، وَأَخَذُوا أَمْوَالَهُمْ، فَأَرْسَلَتْ قُرَيْشٌ إِلَى النَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه وسلم تُنَاشِدُهُ بِاللَّهِ وَالرَّحِمِ لَمَّا أَرْسَلَ، فَمَنْ أَتَاهُ فَهْوَ آمِنٌ، فَأَرْسَلَ النَّبِيُّ صلى الله عليه وسلم إِلَيْهِمْ، فَأَنْزَلَ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى ‏[quran sura="48" aya_start="24" aya_end="24"]{‏وَهُوَ الَّذِي كَفَّ أَيْدِيَهُمْ عَنْكُمْ وَأَيْدِيَكُمْ عَنْهُمْ بِبَطْنِ مَكَّةَ مِنْ بَعْدِ أَنْ أَظْفَرَكُمْ عَلَيْهِمْ‏}‏ حَتَّى بَلَغَ ‏[quran sura="48" aya_start="1" aya_end="1"]{‏الْحَمِيَّةَ حَمِيَّةَ الْجَاهِلِيَّةِ‏}‏ وَكَانَتْ حَمِيَّتُهُمْ أَنَّهُمْ لَمْ يُقِرُّوا أَنَّهُ نَبِيُّ اللَّهِ، وَلَمْ يُقِرُّوا بِبِسْمِ اللَّهِ الرَّحْمَنِ الرَّحِيمِ، وَحَالُوا بَيْنَهُمْ وَبَيْنَ الْبَيْتِ‏.‏
en_text: ‘Abd Allah ibn Muhammad narrated to me: ‘Abd al-Razzaq narrated to us: Ma‘mar informed us. He said: Al-Zuhri informed me. He said: ‘Urwah ibn al-Zubayr informed me, from al-Miswar ibn Makhramah and Marwan, each of whom confirmed the other’s account. He said: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, set out at the time of al-Hudaybiyyah. When they were partway along the road, the Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, said, ‘Khalid ibn al-Walid is at al-Ghamim with a cavalry detachment of Quraysh, acting as their advance guard, so take the road to the right.’ By Allah, Khalid did not notice them until the army’s dust was before him. He set off at a gallop to warn Quraysh. The Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, continued until he reached the mountain pass from which they would descend to them. There his riding camel knelt down. The people said, ‘Get up! Get up!’ but it persisted. They said, ‘Al-Qaswa’ has become stubborn! Al-Qaswa’ has become stubborn!’ The Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, said, ‘Al-Qaswa’ has not become stubborn, and that is not her nature. Rather, the One who restrained the elephant has restrained her.’ Then he said, ‘By the One in Whose hand is my soul, they will not ask me for any proposal that honors the sacred limits of Allah without my granting it to them.’ He urged her on, and she sprang up. He turned away from them and camped at the far end of al-Hudaybiyyah, beside a small pool with little water, from which the people were drawing it a little at a time. The people soon used up its water. The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, was told that they were thirsty. He drew an arrow from his quiver and told them to put it into the pool. By Allah, water kept welling up for them until they left it. While they were there, Budayl ibn Warqa’ al-Khuza‘i arrived with a group of his people from Khuza‘ah. They were trusted advisers of the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, from the people of Tihamah. He said, ‘I left Ka‘b ibn Lu’ayy and ‘Amir ibn Lu’ayy camped at the water sources of al-Hudaybiyyah. With them are the suckling camels and their young. They will fight you and keep you from the House.’ The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, said, ‘We have not come to fight anyone. We have come to perform ‘umrah. War has worn Quraysh out and harmed them. If they wish, I will make a truce with them for a set time, and they will leave me free to meet the people. If I prevail, they may join what the people have joined, if they wish; otherwise, they will have time to recover. If they refuse, then by the One in Whose hand is my soul, I will fight them for this cause until my neck is cut off, and Allah will certainly bring His command to pass.’ Budayl said, ‘I will convey what you say to them.’ He went to Quraysh and said, ‘We have come to you from this man and heard him say something. If you want us to present it to you, we will.’ The foolish among them said, ‘We have no need for you to tell us anything about him.’ But those among them with sound judgment said, ‘Tell us what you heard him say.’ He said, ‘I heard him say such-and-such,’ and told them what the Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, had said. ‘Urwah ibn Mas‘ud stood up and said, ‘My people, am I not like a father to you?’ They said, ‘Yes.’ He said, ‘And am I not like a son to you?’ They said, ‘Yes.’ He said, ‘Do you suspect me?’ They said, ‘No.’ He said, ‘Do you not know that I called the people of ‘Ukaz to join you, but when they held back from me, I came to you with my family, my children, and those who obeyed me?’ They said, ‘Yes.’ He said, ‘This man has offered you a sound proposal. Accept it, and let me go to him.’ They said, ‘Go to him.’ He went to him and began speaking with the Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him. The Prophet said to him much the same as he had said to Budayl. ‘Urwah then said, ‘Muhammad, tell me: if you wipe out your own people, have you ever heard of an Arab who wiped out his people before you? But if the other outcome happens, by Allah, I see faces and a motley group of people who are likely to flee and leave you.’ Abu Bakr said to him, ‘Suck the clitoris of al-Lat! Are we to flee from him and abandon him?’ He asked, ‘Who is that?’ They said, ‘Abu Bakr.’ He said, ‘By the One in Whose hand is my soul, were it not for a favor you once did for me, which I have not repaid, I would answer you.’ As ‘Urwah spoke with the Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, he repeatedly reached for his beard. Al-Mughirah ibn Shu‘bah was standing at the Prophet’s head with a sword and wearing a helmet. Whenever ‘Urwah reached his hand toward the Prophet’s beard, al-Mughirah struck his hand with the flat of the sword and said, ‘Keep your hand away from the beard of the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him.’ ‘Urwah raised his head and asked, ‘Who is this?’ They said, ‘Al-Mughirah ibn Shu‘bah.’ He said, ‘You treacherous one! Am I not still trying to make amends for your treachery?’ In pre-Islamic times, al-Mughirah had accompanied a group of people, killed them, and taken their property. He then came and accepted Islam. The Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, said, ‘As for Islam, I accept it; as for the property, I have nothing to do with it.’ ‘Urwah began watching the Prophet’s companions closely. By Allah, whenever the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, spat, it fell into the hand of one of them, who rubbed it over his face and skin. Whenever he gave them an order, they hastened to carry it out. When he performed ablution, they nearly fought over the water he had used. When he spoke, they lowered their voices in his presence, and out of respect for him they did not stare at him. ‘Urwah returned to his companions and said, ‘My people, by Allah, I have been sent as an envoy to kings. I have been to Caesar, Khosrow, and the Negus. By Allah, I have never seen a king whose companions honored him as much as Muhammad’s companions honor Muhammad, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him. By Allah, whenever he spat, it fell into the hand of one of them, who rubbed it over his face and skin. Whenever he gave them an order, they hastened to carry it out. When he performed ablution, they nearly fought over the water he had used. When he spoke, they lowered their voices in his presence, and out of respect for him they did not stare at him. He has offered you a sound proposal, so accept it.’ A man from Banu Kinanah said, ‘Let me go to him.’ They said, ‘Go to him.’ When he came into view of the Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, and his companions, the Messenger of Allah said, ‘This is so-and-so. He comes from a people who honor sacrificial camels, so send them out to him.’ They sent the camels out, and the people greeted him with the pilgrims’ chant. When he saw that, he said, ‘Glory be to Allah! These people should not be kept from the House.’ When he returned to his companions, he said, ‘I saw that the sacrificial camels had been garlanded and marked. I do not think they should be kept from the House.’ A man among them called Mikraz ibn Hafs stood up and said, ‘Let me go to him.’ They said, ‘Go to him.’ When he came into view of them, the Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, said, ‘This is Mikraz, a wicked man.’ He began speaking with the Prophet. While he was speaking with him, Suhayl ibn ‘Amr arrived. Ma‘mar said: Ayyub informed me, from ‘Ikrimah, that when Suhayl ibn ‘Amr arrived, the Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, said, ‘Your matter has become easier for you.’ Ma‘mar said: Al-Zuhri said in his report: Suhayl ibn ‘Amr came and said, ‘Come, let us write a document between us and you.’ The Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, called for the scribe. The Prophet said, ‘In the name of Allah, the Most Compassionate, the Most Merciful.’ Suhayl said, ‘As for the Most Compassionate, by Allah, I do not know what that is. Write instead, “In Your name, O Allah,” as you used to write.’ The Muslims said, ‘By Allah, we will write only, “In the name of Allah, the Most Compassionate, the Most Merciful.”’ The Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, said, ‘Write, “In Your name, O Allah.”’ Then he said, ‘This is what Muhammad, the Messenger of Allah, has agreed to.’ Suhayl said, ‘By Allah, if we knew that you were the Messenger of Allah, we would not have kept you from the House or fought you. Write “Muhammad ibn ‘Abd Allah” instead.’ The Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, said, ‘By Allah, I am the Messenger of Allah, even if you deny me. Write “Muhammad ibn ‘Abd Allah.”’ Al-Zuhri said: This was because of his words, ‘They will not ask me for any proposal that honors the sacred limits of Allah without my granting it to them.’ The Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, then said to Suhayl, ‘On the condition that you let us reach the House and circumambulate it.’ Suhayl said, ‘By Allah, the Arabs will not say that we were overcome by force. Rather, that will be next year.’ So it was written. Suhayl then said, ‘And on the condition that any man who comes to you from us, even if he follows your religion, you will return him to us.’ The Muslims said, ‘Glory be to Allah! How can someone who has come as a Muslim be returned to the polytheists?’ While they were speaking, Abu Jandal ibn Suhayl ibn ‘Amr came in, dragging his chains. He had escaped from the lower part of Makkah and thrown himself among the Muslims. Suhayl said, ‘This, Muhammad, is the first person I am making a settlement with you about: you must return him to me.’ The Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, said, ‘We have not yet finished the document.’ He said, ‘Then by Allah, I will never make peace with you over anything.’ The Prophet said, ‘Let him go to me.’ He said, ‘I will not let him go to you.’ The Prophet said, ‘Do it, then.’ He said, ‘I will not do it.’ Mikraz said, ‘We have agreed to let him go to you.’ Abu Jandal said, ‘Muslims, am I to be returned to the polytheists when I have come to you as a Muslim? Do you not see what I have suffered?’ He had been tortured severely for Allah’s sake. ‘Umar ibn al-Khattab said: I went to the Prophet of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, and said, ‘Are you truly the Prophet of Allah?’ He said, ‘Yes.’ I said, ‘Are we not upon the truth and our enemy upon falsehood?’ He said, ‘Yes.’ I said, ‘Then why should we accept a humiliating concession in our religion?’ He said, ‘I am the Messenger of Allah, and I do not disobey Him. He is my supporter.’ I said, ‘Did you not used to tell us that we would come to the House and circumambulate it?’ He said, ‘Yes. But did I tell you that we would come to it this year?’ I said, ‘No.’ He said, ‘Then you will come to it and circumambulate it.’’ ‘Umar said: I then went to Abu Bakr and said, ‘Abu Bakr, is he not truly the Prophet of Allah?’ He said, ‘Yes.’ I said, ‘Are we not upon the truth and our enemy upon falsehood?’ He said, ‘Yes.’ I said, ‘Then why should we accept a humiliating concession in our religion?’ He said, ‘Man, he is the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him. He does not disobey his Lord, and He is his supporter. Hold firmly to his course, for by Allah he is upon the truth.’ I said, ‘Did he not used to tell us that we would come to the House and circumambulate it?’ He said, ‘Yes. But did he tell you that you would come to it this year?’ I said, ‘No.’ He said, ‘Then you will come to it and circumambulate it.’’ Al-Zuhri said: ‘Umar said, ‘I did good deeds because of that.’ When the writing of the agreement was finished, the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, said to his companions, ‘Get up, slaughter your sacrificial camels, then shave your heads.’ By Allah, not one man among them got up, even after he had repeated that three times. When no one got up, he went to Umm Salamah and told her what he had encountered from the people. Umm Salamah said, ‘Prophet of Allah, do you want them to do it? Go out, and do not say a word to any of them until you have slaughtered your sacrificial camels and called your barber to shave your head.’ He went out and did not speak to any of them until he had done that: he slaughtered his sacrificial camels and called his barber, who shaved his head. When they saw that, they got up and slaughtered their camels, and they began shaving one another, until some of them nearly killed one another from grief. Then believing women came to him, and Allah Most High revealed, ‘Believers, when believing women come to you as emigrants, examine them’ until the words ‘the marital bonds of disbelieving women’ (60:10). That day ‘Umar divorced two wives he had while they remained in polytheism. Mu‘awiyah ibn Abi Sufyan married one of them, and Safwan ibn Umayyah married the other. Then the Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, returned to Madinah. Abu Basir, a man from Quraysh who was a Muslim, came to him. They sent two men to pursue him and said, ‘Honor the agreement you made with us.’ So he handed Abu Basir over to the two men. They set out with him until they reached Dhu al-Hulayfah, where they stopped to eat some dates they had with them. Abu Basir said to one of the men, ‘By Allah, so-and-so, I think your sword is a fine one.’ The other man drew it and said, ‘Yes, by Allah, it is fine. I have tested it, then tested it again.’ Abu Basir said, ‘Let me see it.’ The man handed it to him, and Abu Basir struck him with it until he was dead. The other man fled until he reached Madinah. He ran into the mosque. When the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, saw him, he said, ‘This man has seen something terrifying.’ When he reached the Prophet, he said, ‘By Allah, my companion has been killed, and I will be killed too.’ Abu Basir then came and said, ‘Prophet of Allah, by Allah, Allah has fulfilled your pledge. You returned me to them, then Allah rescued me from them.’ The Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, said, ‘His mother’s woe! He would kindle a war if he had anyone.’ When Abu Basir heard that, he realized that the Prophet would send him back to them, so he went out until he reached the coast. Abu Jandal ibn Suhayl escaped from them and joined Abu Basir. Every man from Quraysh who became a Muslim and escaped would join Abu Basir, until a group had gathered around him. By Allah, whenever they heard of a caravan belonging to Quraysh setting out for Syria, they intercepted it, killed its men, and took their property. Quraysh then appealed to the Prophet, by Allah and by their kinship, to send for them, promising that whoever came to him would be safe. The Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, sent for them. Then Allah Most High revealed, ‘He is the One who restrained their hands from you and your hands from them in the valley of Makkah, after He had given you victory over them’ until the words ‘the zeal of the time of ignorance’ (48:24; 48:1). Their zeal was that they did not acknowledge that he was the Prophet of Allah, did not acknowledge ‘In the name of Allah, the Most Compassionate, the Most Merciful,’ and prevented them from reaching the House.

reference: Sahih al-Bukhari, hadith 2940, 2941, book 56, باب دُعَاءِ النَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه وسلم إِلَى الإِسْلاَمِ وَالنُّبُوَّةِ، وَأَنْ لاَ يَتَّخِذَ بَعْضُهُمْ بَعْضًا أَرْبَابًا مِنْ دُونِ اللَّهِ
text_original: حَدَّثَنَا إِبْرَاهِيمُ بْنُ حَمْزَةَ، حَدَّثَنَا إِبْرَاهِيمُ بْنُ سَعْدٍ، عَنْ صَالِحِ بْنِ كَيْسَانَ، عَنِ ابْنِ شِهَابٍ، عَنْ عُبَيْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ عُتْبَةَ، عَنْ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ عَبَّاسٍ ـ رضى الله عنهما ـ أَنَّهُ أَخْبَرَهُ أَنَّ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم كَتَبَ إِلَى قَيْصَرَ يَدْعُوهُ إِلَى الإِسْلاَمِ، وَبَعَثَ بِكِتَابِهِ إِلَيْهِ مَعَ دِحْيَةَ الْكَلْبِيِّ، وَأَمَرَهُ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم أَنْ يَدْفَعَهُ إِلَى عَظِيمِ بُصْرَى لِيَدْفَعَهُ إِلَى قَيْصَرَ، وَكَانَ قَيْصَرُ لَمَّا كَشَفَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ جُنُودَ فَارِسَ مَشَى مِنْ حِمْصَ إِلَى إِيلِيَاءَ، شُكْرًا لِمَا أَبْلاَهُ اللَّهُ، فَلَمَّا جَاءَ قَيْصَرَ كِتَابُ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم قَالَ حِينَ قَرَأَهُ الْتَمِسُوا لِي هَا هُنَا أَحَدًا مِنْ قَوْمِهِ لأَسْأَلَهُمْ عَنْ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم‏.‏ قَالَ ابْنُ عَبَّاسٍ فَأَخْبَرَنِي أَبُو سُفْيَانَ، أَنَّهُ كَانَ بِالشَّأْمِ فِي رِجَالٍ مِنْ قُرَيْشٍ، قَدِمُوا تِجَارًا فِي الْمُدَّةِ الَّتِي كَانَتْ بَيْنَ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم وَبَيْنَ كُفَّارِ قُرَيْشٍ، قَالَ أَبُو سُفْيَانَ فَوَجَدَنَا رَسُولُ قَيْصَرَ بِبَعْضِ الشَّأْمِ فَانْطَلَقَ بِي وَبِأَصْحَابِي حَتَّى قَدِمْنَا إِيلِيَاءَ، فَأُدْخِلْنَا عَلَيْهِ، فَإِذَا هُوَ جَالِسٌ فِي مَجْلِسِ مُلْكِهِ وَعَلَيْهِ التَّاجُ، وَإِذَا حَوْلَهُ عُظَمَاءُ الرُّومِ فَقَالَ لِتُرْجُمَانِهِ سَلْهُمْ أَيُّهُمْ أَقْرَبُ نَسَبًا إِلَى هَذَا الرَّجُلِ الَّذِي يَزْعُمُ أَنَّهُ نَبِيٌّ قَالَ أَبُو سُفْيَانَ فَقُلْتُ أَنَا أَقْرَبُهُمْ نَسَبًا‏.‏ قَالَ مَا قَرَابَةُ مَا بَيْنَكَ وَبَيْنَهُ فَقُلْتُ هُوَ ابْنُ عَمِّي، وَلَيْسَ فِي الرَّكْبِ يَوْمَئِذٍ أَحَدٌ مِنْ بَنِي عَبْدِ مَنَافٍ غَيْرِي‏.‏ فَقَالَ قَيْصَرُ أَدْنُوهُ‏.‏ وَأَمَرَ بِأَصْحَابِي فَجُعِلُوا خَلْفَ ظَهْرِي عِنْدَ كَتِفِي، ثُمَّ قَالَ لِتُرْجُمَانِهِ قُلْ لأَصْحَابِهِ إِنِّي سَائِلٌ هَذَا الرَّجُلَ عَنِ الَّذِي يَزْعُمُ أَنَّهُ نَبِيٌّ، فَإِنْ كَذَبَ فَكَذِّبُوهُ‏.‏ قَالَ أَبُو سُفْيَانَ وَاللَّهِ لَوْلاَ الْحَيَاءُ يَوْمَئِذٍ مِنْ أَنْ يَأْثُرَ أَصْحَابِي عَنِّي الْكَذِبَ لَكَذَبْتُهُ حِينَ سَأَلَنِي عَنْهُ، وَلَكِنِّي اسْتَحْيَيْتُ أَنْ يَأْثُرُوا الْكَذِبَ عَنِّي فَصَدَقْتُهُ، ثُمَّ قَالَ لِتُرْجُمَانِهِ قُلْ لَهُ كَيْفَ نَسَبُ هَذَا الرَّجُلِ فِيكُمْ قُلْتُ هُوَ فِينَا ذُو نَسَبٍ‏.‏ قَالَ فَهَلْ قَالَ هَذَا الْقَوْلَ أَحَدٌ مِنْكُمْ قَبْلَهُ قُلْتُ لاَ‏.‏ فَقَالَ كُنْتُمْ تَتَّهِمُونَهُ عَلَى الْكَذِبِ قَبْلَ أَنْ يَقُولَ مَا قَالَ قُلْتُ لاَ‏.‏ قَالَ فَهَلْ كَانَ مِنْ آبَائِهِ مِنْ مَلِكٍ قُلْتُ لاَ‏.‏ قَالَ فَأَشْرَافُ النَّاسِ يَتَّبِعُونَهُ أَمْ ضُعَفَاؤُهُمْ قُلْتُ بَلْ ضُعَفَاؤُهُمْ‏.‏ قَالَ فَيَزِيدُونَ أَوْ يَنْقُصُونَ قُلْتُ بَلْ يَزِيدُونَ‏.‏ قَالَ فَهَلْ يَرْتَدُّ أَحَدٌ سَخْطَةً لِدِينِهِ بَعْدَ أَنْ يَدْخُلَ فِيهِ قُلْتُ لاَ‏.‏ قَالَ فَهَلْ يَغْدِرُ قُلْتُ لاَ، وَنَحْنُ الآنَ مِنْهُ فِي مُدَّةٍ، نَحْنُ نَخَافُ أَنْ يَغْدِرَ‏.‏ قَالَ أَبُو سُفْيَانَ وَلَمْ يُمْكِنِّي كَلِمَةٌ أُدْخِلُ فِيهَا شَيْئًا أَنْتَقِصُهُ بِهِ لاَ أَخَافُ أَنْ تُؤْثَرَ عَنِّي غَيْرُهَا‏.‏ قَالَ فَهَلْ قَاتَلْتُمُوهُ أَوْ قَاتَلَكُمْ قُلْتُ نَعَمْ‏.‏ قَالَ فَكَيْفَ كَانَتْ حَرْبُهُ وَحَرْبُكُمْ قُلْتُ كَانَتْ دُوَلاً وَسِجَالاً، يُدَالُ عَلَيْنَا الْمَرَّةَ وَنُدَالُ عَلَيْهِ الأُخْرَى‏.‏ قَالَ فَمَاذَا يَأْمُرُكُمْ قَالَ يَأْمُرُنَا أَنْ نَعْبُدَ اللَّهَ وَحْدَهُ لاَ نُشْرِكُ بِهِ شَيْئًا، وَيَنْهَانَا عَمَّا كَانَ يَعْبُدُ آبَاؤُنَا، وَيَأْمُرُنَا بِالصَّلاَةِ وَالصَّدَقَةِ وَالْعَفَافِ وَالْوَفَاءِ بِالْعَهْدِ وَأَدَاءِ الأَمَانَةِ‏.‏ فَقَالَ لِتُرْجُمَانِهِ حِينَ قُلْتُ ذَلِكَ لَهُ قُلْ لَهُ إِنِّي سَأَلْتُكَ عَنْ نَسَبِهِ فِيكُمْ، فَزَعَمْتَ أَنَّهُ ذُو نَسَبٍ، وَكَذَلِكَ الرُّسُلُ تُبْعَثُ فِي نَسَبِ قَوْمِهَا، وَسَأَلْتُكَ هَلْ قَالَ أَحَدٌ مِنْكُمْ هَذَا الْقَوْلَ قَبْلَهُ فَزَعَمْتَ أَنْ لاَ، فَقُلْتُ لَوْ كَانَ أَحَدٌ مِنْكُمْ قَالَ هَذَا الْقَوْلَ قَبْلَهُ قُلْتُ رَجُلٌ يَأْتَمُّ بِقَوْلٍ قَدْ قِيلَ قَبْلَهُ‏.‏ وَسَأَلْتُكَ هَلْ كُنْتُمْ تَتَّهِمُونَهُ بِالْكَذِبِ قَبْلَ أَنْ يَقُولَ مَا قَالَ فَزَعَمْتَ أَنْ لاَ، فَعَرَفْتُ أَنَّهُ لَمْ يَكُنْ لِيَدَعَ الْكَذِبَ عَلَى النَّاسِ وَيَكْذِبَ عَلَى اللَّهِ، وَسَأَلْتُكَ هَلْ كَانَ مِنْ آبَائِهِ مِنْ مَلِكٍ فَزَعَمْتَ أَنْ لاَ، فَقُلْتُ لَوْ كَانَ مِنْ آبَائِهِ مَلِكٌ قُلْتُ يَطْلُبُ مُلْكَ آبَائِهِ‏.‏ وَسَأَلْتُكَ أَشْرَافُ النَّاسِ يَتَّبِعُونَهُ أَمْ ضُعَفَاؤُهُمْ فَزَعَمْتَ أَنَّ ضُعَفَاءَهُمُ اتَّبَعُوهُ، وَهُمْ أَتْبَاعُ الرُّسُلِ، وَسَأَلْتُكَ هَلْ يَزِيدُونَ أَوْ يَنْقُصُونَ فَزَعَمْتَ أَنَّهُمْ يَزِيدُونَ، وَكَذَلِكَ الإِيمَانُ حَتَّى يَتِمَّ، وَسَأَلْتُكَ هَلْ يَرْتَدُّ أَحَدٌ سَخْطَةً لِدِينِهِ بَعْدَ أَنْ يَدْخُلَ فِيهِ فَزَعَمْتَ أَنْ لاَ، فَكَذَلِكَ الإِيمَانُ حِينَ تَخْلِطُ بَشَاشَتُهُ الْقُلُوبَ لاَ يَسْخَطُهُ أَحَدٌ، وَسَأَلْتُكَ هَلْ يَغْدِرُ فَزَعَمْتَ أَنْ لاَ، وَكَذَلِكَ الرُّسُلُ لاَ يَغْدِرُونَ‏.‏ وَسَأَلْتُكَ هَلْ قَاتَلْتُمُوهُ وَقَاتَلَكُمْ فَزَعَمْتَ أَنْ قَدْ فَعَلَ، وَأَنَّ حَرْبَكُمْ وَحَرْبَهُ تَكُونُ دُوَلاً، وَيُدَالُ عَلَيْكُمُ الْمَرَّةَ وَتُدَالُونَ عَلَيْهِ الأُخْرَى، وَكَذَلِكَ الرُّسُلُ تُبْتَلَى، وَتَكُونُ لَهَا الْعَاقِبَةُ، وَسَأَلْتُكَ بِمَاذَا يَأْمُرُكُمْ فَزَعَمْتَ أَنَّهُ يَأْمُرُكُمْ أَنْ تَعْبُدُوا اللَّهَ وَلاَ تُشْرِكُوا بِهِ شَيْئًا، وَيَنْهَاكُمْ عَمَّا كَانَ يَعْبُدُ آبَاؤُكُمْ، وَيَأْمُرُكُمْ بِالصَّلاَةِ وَالصِّدْقِ وَالْعَفَافِ وَالْوَفَاءِ بِالْعَهْدِ، وَأَدَاءِ الأَمَانَةِ، قَالَ وَهَذِهِ صِفَةُ النَّبِيِّ، قَدْ كُنْتُ أَعْلَمُ أَنَّهُ خَارِجٌ، وَلَكِنْ لَمْ أَظُنَّ أَنَّهُ مِنْكُمْ، وَإِنْ يَكُ مَا قُلْتَ حَقًّا، فَيُوشِكُ أَنْ يَمْلِكَ مَوْضِعَ قَدَمَىَّ هَاتَيْنِ، وَلَوْ أَرْجُو أَنْ أَخْلُصَ إِلَيْهِ لَتَجَشَّمْتُ لُقِيَّهُ، وَلَوْ كُنْتُ عِنْدَهُ لَغَسَلْتُ قَدَمَيْهِ‏.‏ قَالَ أَبُو سُفْيَانَ ثُمَّ دَعَا بِكِتَابِ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم فَقُرِئَ فَإِذَا فِيهِ ‏"‏ بِسْمِ اللَّهِ الرَّحْمَنِ الرَّحِيمِ مِنْ مُحَمَّدٍ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ وَرَسُولِهِ، إِلَى هِرَقْلَ عَظِيمِ الرُّومِ، سَلاَمٌ عَلَى مَنِ اتَّبَعَ الْهُدَى، أَمَّا بَعْدُ فَإِنِّي أَدْعُوكَ بِدِعَايَةِ الإِسْلاَمِ، أَسْلِمْ تَسْلَمْ، وَأَسْلِمْ يُؤْتِكَ اللَّهُ أَجْرَكَ مَرَّتَيْنِ، فَإِنْ تَوَلَّيْتَ فَعَلَيْكَ إِثْمُ الأَرِيسِيِّينَ وَ[quran sura="3" aya_start="64" aya_end="64"]‏{‏يَا أَهْلَ الْكِتَابِ تَعَالَوْا إِلَى كَلِمَةٍ سَوَاءٍ بَيْنَنَا وَبَيْنَكُمْ أَنْ لاَ نَعْبُدَ إِلاَّ اللَّهَ وَلاَ نُشْرِكَ بِهِ شَيْئًا وَلاَ يَتَّخِذَ بَعْضُنَا بَعْضًا أَرْبَابًا مِنْ دُونِ اللَّهِ فَإِنْ تَوَلَّوْا فَقُولُوا اشْهَدُوا بِأَنَّا مُسْلِمُونَ‏}‏‏"‏‏.‏ قَالَ أَبُو سُفْيَانَ فَلَمَّا أَنْ قَضَى مَقَالَتَهُ، عَلَتْ أَصْوَاتُ الَّذِينَ حَوْلَهُ مِنْ عُظَمَاءِ الرُّومِ، وَكَثُرَ لَغَطُهُمْ، فَلاَ أَدْرِي مَاذَا قَالُوا، وَأُمِرَ بِنَا فَأُخْرِجْنَا، فَلَمَّا أَنْ خَرَجْتُ مَعَ أَصْحَابِي وَخَلَوْتُ بِهِمْ قُلْتُ لَهُمْ لَقَدْ أَمِرَ أَمْرُ ابْنِ أَبِي كَبْشَةَ، هَذَا مَلِكُ بَنِي الأَصْفَرِ يَخَافُهُ، قَالَ أَبُو سُفْيَانَ وَاللَّهِ مَا زِلْتُ ذَلِيلاً مُسْتَيْقِنًا بِأَنَّ أَمْرَهُ سَيَظْهَرُ، حَتَّى أَدْخَلَ اللَّهُ قَلْبِي الإِسْلاَمَ وَأَنَا كَارِهٌ‏.‏
en_text: Ibrahim ibn Hamzah narrated to us: Ibrahim ibn Sa‘d narrated to us, from Salih ibn Kaysan, from Ibn Shihab, from ‘Ubayd Allah ibn ‘Abd Allah ibn ‘Utbah, from ‘Abd Allah ibn ‘Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, who told him that the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, wrote to Caesar, inviting him to Islam. He sent the letter to him with Dihyah al-Kalbi. The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, instructed him to give it to the governor of Busra, who would then deliver it to Caesar. After Allah had driven the Persian forces away from him, Caesar had walked from Hims to Iliya in gratitude for what Allah had granted him. When the letter of the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, reached Caesar, he said after reading it, ‘Find someone here from his people so that I may ask them about the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him.’ Ibn ‘Abbas said: Abu Sufyan informed me that he was in Syria with some men from Quraysh. They had come there as traders during the truce between the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, and the unbelievers of Quraysh. Abu Sufyan said: Caesar’s messenger found us in one part of Syria and took me and my companions with him until we reached Iliya. We were brought in to see Caesar, who was seated in his royal court wearing his crown, with the leading Romans around him. He said to his interpreter, ‘Ask them which of them is closest in kinship to this man who claims to be a prophet.’ Abu Sufyan said: I replied, ‘I am the closest of them in kinship.’ He asked, ‘What is your relationship to him?’ I said, ‘He is my cousin.’ At that time there was no one from Banu ‘Abd Manaf in the travelling party besides me. Caesar said, ‘Bring him closer.’ He ordered my companions to stand behind me, near my shoulders. Then he said to his interpreter, ‘Tell his companions that I will question this man about the one who claims to be a prophet. If he lies, tell me that he is lying.’ Abu Sufyan said: By Allah, had I not felt ashamed that my companions might report a lie from me, I would have lied about him when Caesar questioned me. But I was ashamed that they might report a lie from me, so I told him the truth. Then Caesar said to his interpreter, ‘Ask him: What is this man’s standing among you in terms of lineage?’ I said, ‘He has noble lineage among us.’ He asked, ‘Has anyone among you made this claim before him?’ I said, ‘No.’ He asked, ‘Did you accuse him of lying before he made this claim?’ I said, ‘No.’ He asked, ‘Was any of his forefathers a king?’ I said, ‘No.’ He asked, ‘Do the leading people follow him, or the weak among them?’ I said, ‘Rather, the weak among them.’ He asked, ‘Are they increasing in number or decreasing?’ I said, ‘They are increasing.’ He asked, ‘Does anyone leave his religion out of resentment after entering it?’ I said, ‘No.’ He asked, ‘Does he betray?’ I said, ‘No. We are now in a truce with him, though we fear he may betray us.’ Abu Sufyan said: I could not find a way to add anything against him except that, and I was afraid that something else I said might be reported about me. Caesar asked, ‘Have you fought him, or has he fought you?’ I said, ‘Yes.’ He asked, ‘How has the war between him and you gone?’ I said, ‘It has been alternating: sometimes we have the upper hand, and sometimes he has the upper hand.’ He asked, ‘What does he command you to do?’ I said, ‘He commands us to worship Allah alone and associate nothing with Him; he forbids us from worshipping what our forefathers worshipped; and he commands us to pray, give charity, be chaste, fulfill our covenants, and return what has been entrusted to us.’ When I had said that, Caesar said to his interpreter, ‘Tell him: I asked you about his lineage among you, and you claimed that he has noble lineage. That is how messengers are sent from among the noblest of their people. I asked whether anyone among you had made this claim before him, and you said no. I said that if anyone among you had made this claim before him, I would have thought that he was following a claim made before him. I asked whether you had accused him of lying before he made his claim, and you said no. I therefore know that he would not stop lying to people and then lie about Allah. I asked whether any of his forefathers was a king, and you said no. I said that if one of his forefathers had been a king, I would have thought that he was seeking his forefathers’ kingdom. I asked whether the leading people or the weak among them follow him, and you said that the weak among them follow him. They are the followers of the messengers. I asked whether they are increasing or decreasing, and you said they are increasing. That is how faith grows until it is complete. I asked whether anyone leaves his religion out of resentment after entering it, and you said no. That is how faith is when its joy enters hearts: no one resents it. I asked whether he betrays, and you said no. That is how the messengers are; they do not betray. I asked whether you fought him and he fought you, and you said that it had happened, and that the war between you and him alternates: sometimes you have the upper hand, and sometimes he has the upper hand. That is how the messengers are: they are tested, and the final outcome is theirs. I asked you what he commands you to do, and you said that he commands you to worship Allah and associate nothing with Him, forbids you from worshipping what your forefathers worshipped, and commands you to pray, speak truthfully, be chaste, fulfill your covenants, and return what has been entrusted to you.’ Caesar then said, ‘This is the description of a prophet. I knew that he would appear, but I did not think he would be from among you. If what you have told me is true, he will soon rule the ground beneath these two feet of mine. If I hoped that I could reach him, I would take the trouble to meet him. If I were with him, I would wash his feet.’ Abu Sufyan said: Then Caesar called for the letter of the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, and it was read. It said: ‘In the name of Allah, the Most Compassionate, the Most Merciful. From Muhammad, the servant of Allah and His Messenger, to Heraclius, the great ruler of the Romans. Peace be upon those who follow guidance. To continue: I invite you with the invitation of Islam. Accept Islam and you will be safe. Accept Islam, and Allah will give you your reward twice over. If you turn away, the sin of the Erisiyyin will be upon you. “People of the Scripture, come to a word that is fair between us and you: that we worship none but Allah and associate nothing with Him, and that none of us take others as lords besides Allah. If they turn away, then say, ‘Bear witness that we are Muslims’” (3:64).’ Abu Sufyan said: When Caesar had finished speaking, the voices of the leading Romans around him rose, and their noise grew loud. I do not know what they said. We were ordered out and taken away. When I had left with my companions and was alone with them, I said, ‘The affair of Ibn Abi Kabshah has become great. Even the king of Banu al-Asfar fears him.’ Abu Sufyan said: By Allah, I remained humiliated and certain that his cause would prevail until Allah placed Islam in my heart, though I disliked it.

reference: Sahih al-Bukhari, hadith 3571, book 61, باب عَلاَمَاتِ النُّبُوَّةِ فِي الإِسْلاَمِ
text_original: حَدَّثَنَا أَبُو الْوَلِيدِ، حَدَّثَنَا سَلْمُ بْنُ زَرِيرٍ، سَمِعْتُ أَبَا رَجَاءٍ، قَالَ حَدَّثَنَا عِمْرَانُ بْنُ حُصَيْنٍ، أَنَّهُمْ كَانُوا مَعَ النَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه وسلم فِي مَسِيرٍ، فَأَدْلَجُوا لَيْلَتَهُمْ حَتَّى إِذَا كَانَ وَجْهُ الصُّبْحِ عَرَّسُوا فَغَلَبَتْهُمْ أَعْيُنُهُمْ حَتَّى ارْتَفَعَتِ الشَّمْسُ، فَكَانَ أَوَّلَ مَنِ اسْتَيْقَظَ مِنْ مَنَامِهِ أَبُو بَكْرٍ، وَكَانَ لاَ يُوقَظُ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم مِنْ مَنَامِهِ حَتَّى يَسْتَيْقِظَ، فَاسْتَيْقَظَ عُمَرُ فَقَعَدَ أَبُو بَكْرٍ عِنْدَ رَأْسِهِ فَجَعَلَ يُكَبِّرُ وَيَرْفَعُ صَوْتَهُ، حَتَّى اسْتَيْقَظَ النَّبِيُّ صلى الله عليه وسلم فَنَزَلَ وَصَلَّى بِنَا الْغَدَاةَ، فَاعْتَزَلَ رَجُلٌ مِنَ الْقَوْمِ لَمْ يُصَلِّ مَعَنَا فَلَمَّا انْصَرَفَ قَالَ ‏"‏ يَا فُلاَنُ مَا يَمْنَعُكَ أَنْ تُصَلِّيَ مَعَنَا ‏"‏‏.‏ قَالَ أَصَابَتْنِي جَنَابَةٌ‏.‏ فَأَمَرَهُ أَنْ يَتَيَمَّمَ بِالصَّعِيدِ، ثُمَّ صَلَّى وَجَعَلَنِي رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم فِي رَكُوبٍ بَيْنَ يَدَيْهِ، وَقَدْ عَطِشْنَا عَطَشًا شَدِيدًا فَبَيْنَمَا نَحْنُ نَسِيرُ إِذَا نَحْنُ بِامْرَأَةٍ سَادِلَةٍ رِجْلَيْهَا بَيْنَ مَزَادَتَيْنِ، فَقُلْنَا لَهَا أَيْنَ الْمَاءُ فَقَالَتْ إِنَّهُ لاَ مَاءَ‏.‏ فَقُلْنَا كَمْ بَيْنَ أَهْلِكِ وَبَيْنَ الْمَاءِ قَالَتْ يَوْمٌ وَلَيْلَةٌ‏.‏ فَقُلْنَا انْطَلِقِي إِلَى رَسُولِ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم‏.‏ قَالَتْ وَمَا رَسُولُ اللَّهِ فَلَمْ نُمَلِّكْهَا مِنْ أَمْرِهَا حَتَّى اسْتَقْبَلْنَا بِهَا النَّبِيَّ صلى الله عليه وسلم، فَحَدَّثَتْهُ بِمِثْلِ الَّذِي حَدَّثَتْنَا غَيْرَ أَنَّهَا حَدَّثَتْهُ أَنَّهَا مُؤْتِمَةٌ، فَأَمَرَ بِمَزَادَتَيْهَا فَمَسَحَ فِي الْعَزْلاَوَيْنِ، فَشَرِبْنَا عِطَاشًا أَرْبَعِينَ رَجُلاً حَتَّى رَوِينَا، فَمَلأْنَا كُلَّ قِرْبَةٍ مَعَنَا وَإِدَاوَةٍ، غَيْرَ أَنَّهُ لَمْ نَسْقِ بَعِيرًا وَهْىَ تَكَادُ تَنِضُّ مِنَ الْمِلْءِ ثُمَّ قَالَ ‏"‏ هَاتُوا مَا عِنْدَكُمْ ‏"‏‏.‏ فَجُمِعَ لَهَا مِنَ الْكِسَرِ وَالتَّمْرِ، حَتَّى أَتَتْ أَهْلَهَا قَالَتْ لَقِيتُ أَسْحَرَ النَّاسِ، أَوْ هُوَ نَبِيٌّ كَمَا زَعَمُوا، فَهَدَى اللَّهُ ذَاكَ الصِّرْمَ بِتِلْكَ الْمَرْأَةِ فَأَسْلَمَتْ وَأَسْلَمُوا‏.‏
en_text: Abu al-Walid narrated to us: Salm ibn Zarir narrated to us. I heard Abu Raja’ say: ‘Imran ibn Husayn narrated to us that they were with the Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, on a journey. They travelled through the night. At daybreak they stopped to rest, and sleep overcame them until the sun had risen high. The first to wake from his sleep was Abu Bakr. The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, was not woken from his sleep until he woke by himself. ‘Umar woke, and Abu Bakr sat at the Prophet’s head and began saying “Allah is greatest” and raising his voice until the Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, woke. He got down and led us in the morning prayer. One man from the group stayed apart and did not pray with us. When the Prophet had finished, he said, “So-and-so, what kept you from praying with us?” The man said, “I was in a state of major ritual impurity.” He told him to perform dry ablution with clean earth. Then he prayed. The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, placed me among the riders in front of him. We were extremely thirsty. As we travelled, we came upon a woman with her legs hanging between two water-skins. We asked her, “Where is the water?” She said, “There is no water.” We asked, “How far is it from your family to the water?” She said, “A day and a night.” We said, “Come with us to the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him.” She said, “Who is the Messenger of Allah?” We could not let her decide what to do; we took her to the Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him. She told him what she had told us, except that she also told him she was a widow. He ordered her two water-skins to be brought and rubbed the openings. We drank while thirsty, forty men, until we were satisfied. We filled every waterskin and water-container we had with us, but we did not water a single camel. Her water-skins were almost dripping from being so full. Then he said, “Bring what you have.” They gathered for her the broken pieces of food and dates. When she reached her people, she said, “I have met either the greatest magician of people, or he is a prophet, as they claim.” Through that woman, Allah guided that clan, and she and they embraced Islam.’”

reference: Sahih al-Bukhari, hadith 3578, book 61, باب عَلاَمَاتِ النُّبُوَّةِ فِي الإِسْلاَمِ
text_original: حَدَّثَنَا عَبْدُ اللَّهِ بْنُ يُوسُفَ، أَخْبَرَنَا مَالِكٌ، عَنْ إِسْحَاقَ بْنِ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ أَبِي طَلْحَةَ، أَنَّهُ سَمِعَ أَنَسَ بْنَ مَالِكٍ، يَقُولُ قَالَ أَبُو طَلْحَةَ لأُمِّ سُلَيْمٍ لَقَدْ سَمِعْتُ صَوْتَ، رَسُولِ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم ضَعِيفًا، أَعْرِفُ فِيهِ الْجُوعَ فَهَلْ عِنْدَكِ مِنْ شَىْءٍ قَالَتْ نَعَمْ‏.‏ فَأَخْرَجَتْ أَقْرَاصًا مِنْ شَعِيرٍ، ثُمَّ أَخْرَجَتْ خِمَارًا لَهَا فَلَفَّتِ الْخُبْزَ بِبَعْضِهِ، ثُمَّ دَسَّتْهُ تَحْتَ يَدِي وَلاَثَتْنِي بِبَعْضِهِ، ثُمَّ أَرْسَلَتْنِي إِلَى رَسُولِ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم قَالَ فَذَهَبْتُ بِهِ، فَوَجَدْتُ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم فِي الْمَسْجِدِ وَمَعَهُ النَّاسُ، فَقُمْتُ عَلَيْهِمْ فَقَالَ لِي رَسُولِ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم ‏"‏ آرْسَلَكَ أَبُو طَلْحَةَ ‏"‏‏.‏ فَقُلْتُ نَعَمْ‏.‏ قَالَ بِطَعَامٍ‏.‏ فَقُلْتُ نَعَمْ‏.‏ فَقَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم لِمَنْ مَعَهُ ‏"‏ قُومُوا ‏"‏‏.‏ فَانْطَلَقَ وَانْطَلَقْتُ بَيْنَ أَيْدِيهِمْ حَتَّى جِئْتُ أَبَا طَلْحَةَ فَأَخْبَرْتُهُ‏.‏ فَقَالَ أَبُو طَلْحَةَ يَا أُمَّ سُلَيْمٍ، قَدْ جَاءَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم بِالنَّاسِ، وَلَيْسَ عِنْدَنَا مَا نُطْعِمُهُمْ‏.‏ فَقَالَتِ اللَّهُ وَرَسُولُهُ أَعْلَمُ‏.‏ فَانْطَلَقَ أَبُو طَلْحَةَ حَتَّى لَقِيَ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم، فَأَقْبَلَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم وَأَبُو طَلْحَةَ مَعَهُ، فَقَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم ‏"‏ هَلُمِّي يَا أُمَّ سُلَيْمٍ مَا عِنْدَكِ ‏"‏‏.‏ فَأَتَتْ بِذَلِكَ الْخُبْزِ، فَأَمَرَ بِهِ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم فَفُتَّ، وَعَصَرَتْ أُمُّ سُلَيْمٍ عُكَّةً فَأَدَمَتْهُ، ثُمَّ قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم فِيهِ مَا شَاءَ اللَّهُ أَنْ يَقُولَ، ثُمَّ قَالَ ‏"‏ ائْذَنْ لِعَشَرَةٍ ‏"‏‏.‏ فَأَذِنَ لَهُمْ، فَأَكَلُوا حَتَّى شَبِعُوا ثُمَّ خَرَجُوا، ثُمَّ قَالَ ‏"‏ ائْذَنْ لِعَشَرَةٍ ‏"‏‏.‏ فَأَذِنَ لَهُمْ، فَأَكَلُوا حَتَّى شَبِعُوا ثُمَّ خَرَجُوا، ثُمَّ قَالَ ‏"‏ ائْذَنْ لِعَشَرَةٍ ‏"‏‏.‏ فَأَذِنَ لَهُمْ، فَأَكَلُوا حَتَّى شَبِعُوا ثُمَّ خَرَجُوا ثُمَّ قَالَ ‏"‏ ائْذَنْ لِعَشَرَةٍ ‏"‏‏.‏ فَأَكَلَ الْقَوْمُ كُلُّهُمْ وَشَبِعُوا، وَالْقَوْمُ سَبْعُونَ ـ أَوْ ثَمَانُونَ ـ رَجُلاً‏.‏
en_text: ‘Abd Allah ibn Yusuf narrated to us: Malik informed us, from Ishaq ibn ‘Abd Allah ibn Abi Talhah, who heard Anas ibn Malik say: Abu Talhah said to Umm Sulaym, “I heard the voice of the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, sounding weak. I recognize hunger in it. Do you have anything?” She said, “Yes.” She brought out some barley rolls, then took her head-covering and wrapped part of it around the bread. She tucked it under my arm and tied part of it around me, then sent me to the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him. I went with it and found the Messenger of Allah in the mosque with the people. I stood near them. The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, said to me, “Did Abu Talhah send you?” I said, “Yes.” He asked, “With food?” I said, “Yes.” The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, said to those with him, “Get up.” He set out, and I went ahead of them until I came to Abu Talhah and told him. Abu Talhah said, “Umm Sulaym, the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, has brought the people, and we have nothing to feed them.” She said, “Allah and His Messenger know best.” Abu Talhah went until he met the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him. Then the Messenger of Allah came with Abu Talhah. He said, “Umm Sulaym, bring what you have.” She brought that bread. The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, ordered it to be broken into pieces. Umm Sulaym squeezed out some fat from a small skin-container and used it as a relish. Then the Messenger of Allah said over it whatever Allah willed him to say. Then he said, “Let ten people come in.” Abu Talhah let them in. They ate until they were full, then went out. He said again, “Let ten people come in.” Abu Talhah let them in. They ate until they were full, then went out. He said again, “Let ten people come in.” Abu Talhah let them in. They ate until they were full, then went out. Then he said, “Let ten people come in.” The whole group ate and were satisfied. There were seventy or eighty men.’”

reference: Sahih al-Bukhari, hadith 3581, book 61, باب عَلاَمَاتِ النُّبُوَّةِ فِي الإِسْلاَمِ
text_original: حَدَّثَنَا مُوسَى بْنُ إِسْمَاعِيلَ، حَدَّثَنَا مُعْتَمِرٌ، عَنْ أَبِيهِ، حَدَّثَنَا أَبُو عُثْمَانَ، أَنَّهُ حَدَّثَهُ عَبْدُ الرَّحْمَنِ بْنُ أَبِي بَكْرٍ ـ رضى الله عنهما ـ أَنَّ أَصْحَابَ، الصُّفَّةِ كَانُوا أُنَاسًا فُقَرَاءَ، وَأَنَّ النَّبِيَّ ـ صلى الله عليه وسلم قَالَ مَرَّةً ‏"‏ مَنْ كَانَ عِنْدَهُ طَعَامُ اثْنَيْنِ فَلْيَذْهَبْ بِثَالِثٍ، وَمَنْ كَانَ عِنْدَهُ طَعَامُ أَرْبَعَةٍ فَلْيَذْهَبْ بِخَامِسٍ أَوْ سَادِسٍ ‏"‏‏.‏ أَوْ كَمَا قَالَ، وَأَنَّ أَبَا بَكْرٍ جَاءَ بِثَلاَثَةٍ وَانْطَلَقَ النَّبِيُّ صلى الله عليه وسلم بِعَشَرَةٍ، وَأَبُو بَكْرٍ وَثَلاَثَةً، قَالَ فَهْوَ أَنَا وَأَبِي وَأُمِّي ـ وَلاَ أَدْرِي هَلْ قَالَ امْرَأَتِي وَخَادِمِي ـ بَيْنَ بَيْتِنَا وَبَيْنَ بَيْتِ أَبِي بَكْرٍ، وَأَنَّ أَبَا بَكْرٍ تَعَشَّى عِنْدَ النَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه وسلم ثُمَّ لَبِثَ حَتَّى صَلَّى الْعِشَاءَ، ثُمَّ رَجَعَ فَلَبِثَ حَتَّى تَعَشَّى رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم فَجَاءَ بَعْدَ مَا مَضَى مِنَ اللَّيْلِ مَا شَاءَ اللَّهُ، قَالَتْ لَهُ امْرَأَتُهُ مَا حَبَسَكَ عَنْ أَضْيَافِكَ أَوْ ضَيْفِكَ‏.‏ قَالَ أَوَ عَشَّيْتِهِمْ قَالَتْ أَبَوْا حَتَّى تَجِيءَ، قَدْ عَرَضُوا عَلَيْهِمْ فَغَلَبُوهُمْ، فَذَهَبْتُ فَاخْتَبَأْتُ، فَقَالَ يَا غُنْثَرُ‏.‏ فَجَدَّعَ وَسَبَّ وَقَالَ كُلُوا وَقَالَ لاَ أَطْعَمُهُ أَبَدًا‏.‏ قَالَ وَايْمُ اللَّهِ مَا كُنَّا نَأْخُذُ مِنَ اللُّقْمَةِ إِلاَّ رَبَا مِنْ أَسْفَلِهَا أَكْثَرُ مِنْهَا حَتَّى شَبِعُوا، وَصَارَتْ أَكْثَرَ مِمَّا كَانَتْ قَبْلُ، فَنَظَرَ أَبُو بَكْرٍ فَإِذَا شَىْءٌ أَوْ أَكْثَرُ قَالَ لاِمْرَأَتِهِ يَا أُخْتَ بَنِي فِرَاسٍ‏.‏ قَالَتْ لاَ وَقُرَّةِ عَيْنِي لَهْىَ الآنَ أَكْثَرُ مِمَّا قَبْلُ بِثَلاَثِ مَرَّاتٍ‏.‏ فَأَكَلَ مِنْهَا أَبُو بَكْرٍ، وَقَالَ إِنَّمَا كَانَ الشَّيْطَانُ ـ يَعْنِي يَمِينَهُ ـ ثُمَّ أَكَلَ مِنْهَا لُقْمَةً، ثُمَّ حَمَلَهَا إِلَى النَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه وسلم فَأَصْبَحَتْ عِنْدَهُ‏.‏ وَكَانَ بَيْنَنَا وَبَيْنَ قَوْمٍ عَهْدٌ، فَمَضَى الأَجَلُ، فَتَفَرَّقْنَا اثْنَا عَشَرَ رَجُلاً مَعَ كُلِّ رَجُلٍ مِنْهُمْ أُنَاسٌ‏.‏ اللَّهُ أَعْلَمُ كَمْ مَعَ كُلِّ رَجُلٍ، غَيْرَ أَنَّهُ بَعَثَ مَعَهُمْ، قَالَ أَكَلُوا مِنْهَا أَجْمَعُونَ‏.‏ أَوْ كَمَا قَالَ‏.‏ وَغَيْرُهُ يَقُولُ فَعَرَفْنَا مِنْ الْعِرَافَةِ
en_text: Musa ibn Isma‘il narrated to us: Mu‘tamir narrated to us, from his father. Abu ‘Uthman narrated to us that ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Bakr, may Allah be pleased with them both, told him that the people of the Suffah were poor. The Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, once said, “Whoever has food for two should take a third person with him, and whoever has food for four should take a fifth or a sixth,” or words to that effect. Abu Bakr came with three people, and the Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, went out with ten. Abu Bakr and three people [also came]. The narrator said: I was one of them, along with my father and my mother. I do not know whether he also said my wife and my servant. We were between our house and Abu Bakr’s house. Abu Bakr ate the evening meal with the Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, then stayed until he had prayed the night prayer. He returned and stayed until the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, had eaten the evening meal. He came back after as much of the night had passed as Allah willed. His wife said to him, “What kept you from your guests?” He asked, “Have you not served them their evening meal?” She said, “They refused until you came. They offered it to them, but they refused.” I went away and hid. Abu Bakr said, “You fool!” He rebuked and insulted me, then said, “Eat!” and swore, “By Allah, I will never eat it.” By Allah, whenever we took a morsel, the food grew from underneath it, becoming more than it had been, until they were full. It had become more than before. Abu Bakr looked and saw that it was as much as before, or more. He said to his wife, “Sister of Banu Firas, is it more?” She said, “No, by the comfort of my eyes, it is now three times more than it was before.” Abu Bakr ate some of it and said, “That oath was from Satan”—meaning his own oath. Then he ate a morsel and carried the food to the Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him. It was still with him in the morning. There was a truce between us and a people, and its term ended. We separated into twelve groups, with people accompanying each man. Allah knows how many were with each man. The narrator said that he sent the food with them, and they all ate from it, or words to that effect. Another narrator says, “We knew that through the group leaders.”

reference: Sahih al-Bukhari, hadith 3827, book 63, باب حَدِيثُ زَيْدِ بْنِ عَمْرِو بْنِ نُفَيْلٍ
